35: The auto-generated `jac.toml` for a `--kind web-static` project looks like:
36: 
37: ```toml
38: [project]
39: name = "myapp"
40: version = "1.0.0"
41: description = "Jac client application: myapp"
42: entry-point = "main.jac"
43: 
44: [dependencies.npm]
45: jac-client-node = "1.0.7"
46: 
47: [serve]
48: base_route_app = "app"
49: 
50: [client]
51: ```
52: 
53: You typically don't need to modify this file until you add dependencies or customize settings.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## Configuration Sections
58: 
59: ### [project]
60: 
61: Project metadata. `entry-point` drives `jac run`. `jac-version` pins the Jac toolchain the project targets: `jac create` stamps it automatically, and `jac start --scale` uses it to select the pod runtime (see [jac-version](#jac-version) below). Publishing fields (`license`, `readme`, `keywords`, `requires-python`, `authors`, `maintainers`, and `[project.include]`) are used by `jac build --as wheel` when building a distributable wheel. All publishing fields are optional -- a project that is never published only needs `name`.
62: 
63: ```toml
64: [project]
65: name = "myapp"
66: version = "1.0.0"
67: description = "My Jac application"
68: entry-point = "main.jac"
69: kind = "service"   # drives `jac run` (omit to infer from the entry-point)
70: jac-version = "==0.34.3"   # stamped by `jac create`; widen to `>=`, `<=`, or a range
71: 
72: # Publishing metadata -- only needed to run `jac build --as wheel`
73: license = "MIT"
74: readme = "README.md"
75: requires-python = ">=3.12"
76: keywords = ["jac", "ai"]
77: authors = [{ name = "Your Name", email = "you@example.com" }]
78: maintainers = [{ name = "Another Person", email = "them@example.com" }]
79: 
80: [project.urls]
81: homepage = "https://example.com"
82: repository = "https://github.com/user/repo"
83: ```
84: 
85: | Field | Type | Description |
86: |-------|------|-------------|
87: | `name` | string | Project / PyPI package name (required) |
88: | `version` | string | Semantic version (default: `0.1.0`) |
89: | `description` | string | One-line summary (also shown on PyPI) |
90: | `entry-point` | string | Main file for `jac run` (default: `main.jac`) |
91: | `kind` | string | Project kind that drives `jac run` dispatch (execute / serve / build). Empty = inferred from the entry-point codespace. One of: `cli`, `cli-native`, `native-binary`, `native-lib`, `service`, `service-mesh`, `py-package`, `js-package`, `web-app`, `web-static`, `desktop`, `mobile` |
92: | `jac-version` | string | Jac toolchain version the project targets, as a PEP 440-style specifier. `jac create` stamps `==<current>`; at `jac start --scale` the pod runtime binary, admin console, and base image are all taken from the release that satisfies it, and the deploy aborts if none does. See [jac-version](#jac-version). |
93: | `license` | string | SPDX license identifier (e.g. `"MIT"`) |
94: | `readme` | string | Path to README file (default: `README.md`) |
95: | `requires-python` | string | Minimum Python version (e.g. `">=3.12"`) |
96: | `keywords` | list | Search keywords shown on PyPI |
97: | `authors` | list of `{name, email}` | Package authors |
98: | `maintainers` | list of `{name, email}` | Package maintainers |
99: | `urls` | table | Links shown on PyPI (declared under `[project.urls]`) |
100: 
101: > **Note:** `authors` and `maintainers` also accept a plain string form (`authors = ["Your Name"]`), but the `{ name, email }` table form is recommended -- it is what published packages' `jac.toml` files use and what PyPI renders. See [`[project.include]`](#projectinclude) for controlling which files land in the wheel.
102: 
103: #### jac-version
104: 
105: `jac-version` records which Jac toolchain the project targets, written as a PEP 440-style specifier. Since the `jac` toolchain does not guarantee backward compatibility across versions (breaking changes ship as clean breaks), `jac create` stamps the **exact** version you created the project with:
106: 
107: ```toml
108: jac-version = "==0.34.3"
109: ```
110: 
111: You can widen or move it by editing the value -- `>=0.34.3`, `<=0.34.3`, `>=0.34,<0.35`, `~=0.34.3`, or a bare `0.34.3` (same as `==`).
112: 
113: At deploy time (`jac start --scale`), the pin selects the **pod runtime**: the deployer downloads the released `jac` binary, admin console, and base image from the release that satisfies `jac-version` and ships them to the pods, so the app runs on the toolchain it was built against -- not on whatever `latest` happens to be. Resolution rules:
114: 
115: - **Unset** -> the latest published release.
116: - **Exact pin** (`==X` / `X`) -> the `vX` release.
117: - **Range** -> the newest published release that satisfies it.
118: - **No published release satisfies the pin** (or the matching release lacks the pod's CPU arch or a `jac-*` asset) -> the deploy **aborts** with an error naming the pin; a pinned deploy never silently ships a different version. Fix or remove `jac-version` to proceed.
119: 
120: The pin is honored only on the default (stable) channel; the `[dev]`, `[experimental]`, and `JAC_SCALE_BINARY_PATH` (local) channels select the pod binary by their own rules and ignore it.
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ### [dependencies]
125: 
126: Python/PyPI packages:
127: 
128: ```toml
129: [dependencies]
130: requests = ">=2.28.0"
131: numpy = "1.24.0"
132: byllm = ">=0.4.8"
133: 
134: [dev-dependencies]
135: pytest = ">=8.0.0"
136: 
137: [dependencies.git]
138: my-lib = { git = "https://github.com/user/repo.git", branch = "main" }
139: 
140: [dependencies.system]
141: git = "*"
142: ffmpeg = "*"
143: ```
144: 
145: `[dependencies.system]` declares OS (apt) packages your app needs at runtime. On a `jac-scale` Kubernetes deploy they are installed into the service container at startup (Debian only; keys are apt package names). See [System Dependencies](../plugins/jac-scale-kubernetes.md#system-dependencies).

149: | Format | Example | Meaning |

{"file_path": "/workspace/docs/plan.md", "content": "# Rentora backend plan

## Goal

Headless graph backend for Rentora, a small property-management service, on Jac 0.36.1. It has no JSX, no browser UI and no external AI. An owner can:

- add a property with unit numbers
- register a tenant into a unit, which creates the unit and a lease if needed and refuses duplicate phones
- list properties, units, tenants and tickets
- match a tenant by phone
- dispatch and resolve tickets
- delete properties

## Module relationships

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M1["services/graph/models.jac"]
    M2["services/graph/localdb.jac"]
    M3["services/graph/crud.jac"]
    M4["services/graph/actions.jac"]
    M5["main.jac"]
    M1 --> M3
    M2 --> M3
    M1 --> M4
    M3 --> M5
    M4 --> M5
```

Each arrow points from a provider to the module that imports it.

## Frontend modules (.jac)

(none: this is a backend-only service)

## Backend modules (.jac)

- `services/graph/models.jac`: the graph schema.
  - Enums: EventType and UrgencyLevel, with a sem description on each member.
  - Nodes: Property, Unit, Lease, Tenant, Ticket and Vendor.
  - Edges: HasUnit, HasLease, HasTenant, HasTicket, Services and AssignedTo.
  - Graph shape: root -> Property -HasUnit-> Unit -HasLease-> Lease -HasTenant-> Tenant; Unit -HasTicket-> Ticket; Property -Services-> Vendor.
- `services/graph/localdb.jac`: SQLite log store built on stdlib sqlite3/json/os/datetime.
  - Database path: `<cwd>/.jac/data/app.db`. The process only reads and writes this runtime file; agents do not edit it.
  - Tables: sms_messages, walker_logs and notifications.
  - Public functions: log_sms, get_sms_history, log_walker_run, create_notification, get_notifications, db_insert, db_find and check_db_health.
- `services/graph/crud.jac`: walkers list_properties, list_units, list_tickets, list_vendors, register_tenant, db_health, list_tenants, add_property_node, delete_tenant_node, delete_property_node and match_tenant.
- `services/graph/actions.jac`: walkers approve_dispatch and resolve_ticket. Each finds a ticket by ticket_id under a property's units and marks it dispatched or resolved.
- `main.jac`: a docstring and the re-export imports of the crud and action walkers, nothing else.

## Public interfaces

### services/graph/models.jac

- enum EventType { MAINTENANCE, PAYMENT, LEASE, COMPLAINT, INQUIRY }
- enum UrgencyLevel { LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL }
- node Property { name, address, city, state, zip_code: str = "" }
- node Unit { number: str = ""; bedrooms: int = 1; bathrooms: int = 1; sq_ft: int = 0; status: str = "occupied" }
- node Lease { start_date, end_date: str = ""; rent_amount: float = 0.0; deposit: float = 0.0; status: str = "active" }
- node Tenant { name, phone, email: str = ""; payment_status: str = "current"; move_in_date: str = "" }
- node Ticket
  - str fields defaulting to "": ticket_id, category, description, ai_summary, ai_diagnosis, recommended_action, tenant_reply, owner_alert, created_at, resolved_at, vendor_name
  - urgency: str = "medium"
  - status: str = "open"
  - estimated_cost: float = 0.0
- node Vendor { name, category, phone, email: str = ""; rating: float = 0.0; avg_cost: float = 0.0; available: bool = True }
- edge Services { jobs_completed: int = 0; total_spent: float = 0.0; last_service_date: str = "" }
- edges with no fields: HasUnit, HasLease, HasTenant, HasTicket, AssignedTo

### services/graph/localdb.jac

- def:pub log_sms(from_number: str, to_number: str, body: str, direction: str, sid: str = "", unit_id: str = "", tenant_name: str = "") -> dict
- def:pub get_sms_history(phone: str = "", limit_count: int = 50) -> list
- def:pub log_walker_run(walker_name: str, unit_id: str, input_data: dict, output_data: dict, duration_ms: int = 0) -> dict
- def:pub create_notification(notification_type: str, payload: dict, ticket_id: str = "") -> dict
- def:pub get_notifications(unread_only: bool = True, limit_count: int = 20) -> list
- def:pub db_insert(collection: str, doc: dict) -> dict
- def:pub db_find(collection: str, query: dict = {}, limit_count: int = 50) -> list
- def:pub check_db_health() -> dict
  - success: {ok: True, backend: "sqlite", path, tables}
  - failure: {ok: False, backend: "sqlite", path}

### services/graph/crud.jac

- walker list_properties { can list_all with Root entry; }
  - reports one list of {id, name, address, city, state, unit_count}
- walker list_units { can start with Root entry; can gather with Property entry; }
  - reports one dict per unit
- walker list_tickets { start: Root, at_property: Property, at_unit: Unit }
  - reports one dict per ticket
- walker list_vendors { start: Root, at_property: Property }
- walker register_tenant
  - fields: tenant_name, tenant_phone, tenant_email, unit_number, rent_amount: float, lease_start, lease_end, property_name
  - abilities: start (Root entry), find_unit (Property entry)
  - reports {status: "registered" or "already_registered", tenant, phone, unit, property, id}
- walker db_health { can check with Root entry; }
  - reports {database, graph_store: "ok"}
- walker list_tenants { can list_all with Root entry; }
  - reports one list of {id, full_name, phone_number, unit_number, property_id, property_name, rent, lease_end}
- walker add_property_node { has name, address: str; has unit_numbers: list = []; can create with Root entry; }
  - reports {status: "created", id, property, units}
- walker delete_tenant_node { has tenant_id; start, at_property, not_found (Root exit) }
- walker delete_property_node { has property_id; can start with Root entry; }
  - reports {status: "deleted"} or {status: "not_found"}
- walker match_tenant { has phone; start, at_property, not_found (Root exit) }
  - reports {matched: True, tenant_name, property_name, unit} or {matched: False}

### services/graph/actions.jac

- walker approve_dispatch { has ticket_id; start (Root), at_property (Property), at_unit (Unit) }
  - reports {ticket_id, status: "dispatched", vendor_name, unit, tenant_reply, owner_alert, estimated_cost}
- walker resolve_ticket { has ticket_id; same abilities }
  - reports {ticket_id, status: "resolved", resolved_at}

### main.jac

Re-exports the 11 crud walkers and the 2 action walkers.

## Scaffold write order

1. docs/plan.md
2. jac.toml (support file)
3. services/graph/models.jac
4. services/graph/localdb.jac
5. services/graph/crud.jac
6. services/graph/actions.jac
7. main.jac

In the scaffold phase every function and ability body is `raise NotImplementedError();`. The models need no bodies, so they are complete when written.

## Verification

- Run `jac check main.jac`.
- Run `jac test` on tests/test_rentora.jac, which imports the walkers from main and the node/edge types from services.graph.models.
- The tests cover this flow: add property -> register tenant (including a duplicate) -> list and match (including an unknown phone) -> attach ticket -> dispatch -> resolve -> delete property (including an unknown id).
- Route: API only.
"}

# Configuration Reference

The `jac.toml` file is the central configuration for Jac projects -- similar to `pyproject.toml` in Python or `package.json` in Node.js. It defines project metadata (name, version, entry point), manages dependencies (both PyPI and npm packages), sets defaults for CLI commands (test verbosity, server port, lint rules), configures built-in capabilities (LLM models, deployment targets), and supports environment-specific profiles (development vs. production).

You typically don't need to edit `jac.toml` manually for basic projects. The `jac create` command generates one with sensible defaults, and commands like `jac install <pkg>` and `jac config set` modify it for you. But understanding the full configuration surface is valuable when you need to customize build behavior, configure LLM providers, set up lint rules, or manage deployment settings.

`jac` commands locate `jac.toml` by walking up from the current working directory. The only exception is `jac install -e <path>`, which reads `jac.toml` from the resolved `<path>` so editable installs work from anywhere.

## Creating a Project

```bash
# Basic project
jac create myapp
cd myapp

# Full-stack web app (recommended for web development)
jac create myapp --kind web-static
cd myapp
```

This creates a `jac.toml` with default settings. When using `--kind web-static`, the scaffolded project includes:

```
myapp/
├── main.jac                  # Entry point with the client app

... (899 lines omitted) ...


### Scale: Webhooks

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Secret for webhook HMAC signatures |
| `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_HEADER` | Header name for signature |
| `WEBHOOK_VERIFY_SIGNATURE` | Enable signature verification |
| `WEBHOOK_API_KEY_EXPIRY_DAYS` | API key expiry in days |

### Scale: Kubernetes

Deployment settings (app name, namespace, node port, CPU/memory requests and limits, health probes) are configured in `jac.toml` under `[scale.kubernetes]` -- see the [Kubernetes reference](../plugins/jac-scale-kubernetes.md). At deploy time, jac-scale injects these variables into every pod:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `K8S_APP_NAME` | Application name (used by observability and admin tooling inside the pod) |
| `K8S_NAMESPACE` | Namespace the workload runs in |

---

## See Also

- [CLI Reference](../cli/index.md) - Command-line interface documentation
- [Publishing Packages](../publishing.md) - Building and uploading wheels to PyPI

35: The auto-generated `jac.toml` for a `--kind web-static` project looks like:
36: 
37: ```toml
38: [project]
39: name = "myapp"
40: version = "1.0.0"
41: description = "Jac client application: myapp"
42: entry-point = "main.jac"
43: 
44: [dependencies.npm]
45: jac-client-node = "1.0.7"
46: 
47: [serve]
48: base_route_app = "app"
49: 
50: [client]
51: ```
52: 
53: You typically don't need to modify this file until you add dependencies or customize settings.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## Configuration Sections
58: 
59: ### [project]
60: 
61: Project metadata. `entry-point` drives `jac run`. `jac-version` pins the Jac toolchain the project targets: `jac create` stamps it automatically, and `jac start --scale` uses it to select the pod runtime (see [jac-version](#jac-version) below). Publishing fields (`license`, `readme`, `keywords`, `requires-python`, `authors`, `maintainers`, and `[project.include]`) are used by `jac build --as wheel` when building a distributable wheel. All publishing fields are optional -- a project that is never published only needs `name`.
62: 
63: ```toml
64: [project]
65: name = "myapp"
66: version = "1.0.0"
67: description = "My Jac application"
68: entry-point = "main.jac"
69: kind = "service"   # drives `jac run` (omit to infer from the entry-point)
70: jac-version = "==0.34.3"   # stamped by `jac create`; widen to `>=`, `<=`, or a range
71: 
72: # Publishing metadata -- only needed to run `jac build --as wheel`
73: license = "MIT"
74: readme = "README.md"
75: requires-python = ">=3.12"
76: keywords = ["jac", "ai"]
77: authors = [{ name = "Your Name", email = "you@example.com" }]
78: maintainers = [{ name = "Another Person", email = "them@example.com" }]
79: 
80: [project.urls]
81: homepage = "https://example.com"
82: repository = "https://github.com/user/repo"
83: ```
84: 
85: | Field | Type | Description |
86: |-------|------|-------------|
87: | `name` | string | Project / PyPI package name (required) |
88: | `version` | string | Semantic version (default: `0.1.0`) |
89: | `description` | string | One-line summary (also shown on PyPI) |
90: | `entry-point` | string | Main file for `jac run` (default: `main.jac`) |
91: | `kind` | string | Project kind that drives `jac run` dispatch (execute / serve / build). Empty = inferred from the entry-point codespace. One of: `cli`, `cli-native`, `native-binary`, `native-lib`, `service`, `service-mesh`, `py-package`, `js-package`, `web-app`, `web-static`, `desktop`, `mobile` |
92: | `jac-version` | string | Jac toolchain version the project targets, as a PEP 440-style specifier. `jac create` stamps `==<current>`; at `jac start --scale` the pod runtime binary, admin console, and base image are all taken from the release that satisfies it, and the deploy aborts if none does. See [jac-version](#jac-version). |
93: | `license` | string | SPDX license identifier (e.g. `"MIT"`) |
94: | `readme` | string | Path to README file (default: `README.md`) |
95: | `requires-python` | string | Minimum Python version (e.g. `">=3.12"`) |
96: | `keywords` | list | Search keywords shown on PyPI |
97: | `authors` | list of `{name, email}` | Package authors |
98: | `maintainers` | list of `{name, email}` | Package maintainers |
99: | `urls` | table | Links shown on PyPI (declared under `[project.urls]`) |
100: 
101: > **Note:** `authors` and `maintainers` also accept a plain string form (`authors = ["Your Name"]`), but the `{ name, email }` table form is recommended -- it is what published packages' `jac.toml` files use and what PyPI renders. See [`[project.include]`](#projectinclude) for controlling which files land in the wheel.
102: 
103: #### jac-version
104: 
105: `jac-version` records which Jac toolchain the project targets, written as a PEP 440-style specifier. Since the `jac` toolchain does not guarantee backward compatibility across versions (breaking changes ship as clean breaks), `jac create` stamps the **exact** version you created the project with:
106: 
107: ```toml
108: jac-version = "==0.34.3"
109: ```
110: 
111: You can widen or move it by editing the value -- `>=0.34.3`, `<=0.34.3`, `>=0.34,<0.35`, `~=0.34.3`, or a bare `0.34.3` (same as `==`).
112: 
113: At deploy time (`jac start --scale`), the pin selects the **pod runtime**: the deployer downloads the released `jac` binary, admin console, and base image from the release that satisfies `jac-version` and ships them to the pods, so the app runs on the toolchain it was built against -- not on whatever `latest` happens to be. Resolution rules:
114: 
115: - **Unset** -> the latest published release.
116: - **Exact pin** (`==X` / `X`) -> the `vX` release.
117: - **Range** -> the newest published release that satisfies it.
118: - **No published release satisfies the pin** (or the matching release lacks the pod's CPU arch or a `jac-*` asset) -> the deploy **aborts** with an error naming the pin; a pinned deploy never silently ships a different version. Fix or remove `jac-version` to proceed.
119: 
120: The pin is honored only on the default (stable) channel; the `[dev]`, `[experimental]`, and `JAC_SCALE_BINARY_PATH` (local) channels select the pod binary by their own rules and ignore it.
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ### [dependencies]
125: 
126: Python/PyPI packages:
127: 
128: ```toml
129: [dependencies]
130: requests = ">=2.28.0"
131: numpy = "1.24.0"
132: byllm = ">=0.4.8"
133: 
134: [dev-dependencies]
135: pytest = ">=8.0.0"
136: 
137: [dependencies.git]
138: my-lib = { git = "https://github.com/user/repo.git", branch = "main" }
139: 
140: [dependencies.system]
141: git = "*"
142: ffmpeg = "*"
143: ```
144: 
145: `[dependencies.system]` declares OS (apt) packages your app needs at runtime. On a `jac-scale` Kubernetes deploy they are installed into the service container at startup (Debian only; keys are apt package names). See [System Dependencies](../plugins/jac-scale-kubernetes.md#system-dependencies).
146: 
147: **Version specifiers:**
148: 
149: | Format | Example | Meaning |
150: |--------|---------|---------|

## Goal

Build the headless memory backend for RepoGhost, a tool that turns a code repository plus meeting notes into an engineering plan. Put the shared data objects in app/models/core.jac (repo selection, chat message, decision, blocker, file match, ownership guess, meeting summary), the workflow objects in app/models/workflow.jac (workflow mode, trace step, request, run state, planning insight, execution planning context), and the result objects in app/models/outputs.jac (repo summary, task, action plan, generated ticket, handoff, standup, review scope, graph views, docs sync result, query answer, the combined workflow result bundle and the UI view-state record), reusing the core and workflow objects. Then write app/services/memory_store.jac, an in-memory store with remember_session (record a workflow request with the bundle's action-plan headline), recent_session_runs, update_project_memory (keep the decision, blocker and ticket titles from a bundle per repository path) and get_project_memory (return an empty default for unknown repositories; an empty path means the default key). main.jac only imports the four memory operations so the service exposes them.

# Configuration Reference

The `jac.toml` file is the central configuration for Jac projects -- similar to `pyproject.toml` in Python or `package.json` in Node.js. It defines project metadata (name, version, entry point), manages dependencies (both PyPI and npm packages), sets defaults for CLI commands (test verbosity, server port, lint rules), configures built-in capabilities (LLM models, deployment targets), and supports environment-specific profiles (development vs. production).

You typically don't need to edit `jac.toml` manually for basic projects. The `jac create` command generates one with sensible defaults, and commands like `jac install <pkg>` and `jac config set` modify it for you. But understanding the full configuration surface is valuable when you need to customize build behavior, configure LLM providers, set up lint rules, or manage deployment settings.

`jac` commands locate `jac.toml` by walking up from the current working directory. The only exception is `jac install -e <path>`, which reads `jac.toml` from the resolved `<path>` so editable installs work from anywhere.

## Creating a Project

```bash
# Basic project
jac create myapp
cd myapp

# Full-stack web app (recommended for web development)
jac create myapp --kind web-static
cd myapp
```

This creates a `jac.toml` with default settings. When using `--kind web-static`, the scaffolded project includes:

```
myapp/
├── main.jac                  # Entry point with the client app

... (899 lines omitted) ...


### Scale: Webhooks

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Secret for webhook HMAC signatures |
| `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_HEADER` | Header name for signature |
| `WEBHOOK_VERIFY_SIGNATURE` | Enable signature verification |
| `WEBHOOK_API_KEY_EXPIRY_DAYS` | API key expiry in days |

### Scale: Kubernetes

Deployment settings (app name, namespace, node port, CPU/memory requests and limits, health probes) are configured in `jac.toml` under `[scale.kubernetes]` -- see the [Kubernetes reference](../plugins/jac-scale-kubernetes.md). At deploy time, jac-scale injects these variables into every pod:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `K8S_APP_NAME` | Application name (used by observability and admin tooling inside the pod) |
| `K8S_NAMESPACE` | Namespace the workload runs in |

---

## See Also

- [CLI Reference](../cli/index.md) - Command-line interface documentation
- [Publishing Packages](../publishing.md) - Building and uploading wheels to PyPI

20: 
21: This creates a `jac.toml` with default settings. When using `--kind web-static`, the scaffolded project includes:
22: 
23: ```
24: myapp/
25: ├── main.jac                  # Entry point with the client app
26: ├── jac.toml                  # Project configuration (auto-generated)
27: ├── components/
28: │   └── Button.jac         # Example client component
29: ├── assets/                   # Static assets
30: ├── README.md
31: ├── AGENTS.md                 # Points AI coding agents at `jac guide`
32: └── .gitignore

34: 
35: The auto-generated `jac.toml` for a `--kind web-static` project looks like:
36: 
37: ```toml
38: [project]
39: name = "myapp"
40: version = "1.0.0"
41: description = "Jac client application: myapp"
42: entry-point = "main.jac"
43: 
44: [dependencies.npm]
45: jac-client-node = "1.0.7"
46: 
47: [serve]
48: base_route_app = "app"
49: 
50: [client]
51: ```
52: 
53: You typically don't need to modify this file until you add dependencies or customize settings.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## Configuration Sections
58: 
59: ### [project]
60: 
61: Project metadata. `entry-point` drives `jac run`. `jac-version` pins the Jac toolchain the project targets: `jac create` stamps it automatically, and `jac start --scale` uses it to select the pod runtime (see [jac-version](#jac-version) below). Publishing fields (`license`, `readme`, `keywords`, `requires-python`, `authors`, `maintainers`, and `[project.include]`) are used by `jac build --as wheel` when building a distributable wheel. All publishing fields are optional -- a project that is never published only needs `name`.
62: 
63: ```toml
64: [project]
65: name = "myapp"
66: version = "1.0.0"
67: description = "My Jac application"
68: entry-point = "main.jac"
69: kind = "service"   # drives `jac run` (omit to infer from the entry-point)
70: jac-version = "==0.34.3"   # stamped by `jac create`; widen to `>=`, `<=`, or a range
71: 
72: # Publishing metadata -- only needed to run `jac build --as wheel`
73: license = "MIT"
74: readme = "README.md"
75: requires-python = ">=3.12"
76: keywords = ["jac", "ai"]
77: authors = [{ name = "Your Name", email = "you@example.com" }]
78: maintainers = [{ name = "Another Person", email = "them@example.com" }]
79: 
80: [project.urls]
81: homepage = "https://example.com"
82: repository = "https://github.com/user/repo"
83: ```
84: 
85: | Field | Type | Description |
86: |-------|------|-------------|
87: | `name` | string | Project / PyPI package name (required) |
88: | `version` | string | Semantic version (default: `0.1.0`) |
89: | `description` | string | One-line summary (also shown on PyPI) |
90: | `entry-point` | string | Main file for `jac run` (default: `main.jac`) |
91: | `kind` | string | Project kind that drives `jac run` dispatch (execute / serve / build). Empty = inferred from the entry-point codespace. One of: `cli`, `cli-native`, `native-binary`, `native-lib`, `service`, `service-mesh`, `py-package`, `js-package`, `web-app`, `web-static`, `desktop`, `mobile` |
92: | `jac-version` | string | Jac toolchain version the project targets, as a PEP 440-style specifier. `jac create` stamps `==<current>`; at `jac start --scale` the pod runtime binary, admin console, and base image are all taken from the release that satisfies it, and the deploy aborts if none does. See [jac-version](#jac-version). |
93: | `license` | string | SPDX license identifier (e.g. `"MIT"`) |
94: | `readme` | string | Path to README file (default: `README.md`) |
95: | `requires-python` | string | Minimum Python version (e.g. `">=3.12"`) |
96: | `keywords` | list | Search keywords shown on PyPI |
97: | `authors` | list of `{name, email}` | Package authors |
98: | `maintainers` | list of `{name, email}` | Package maintainers |
99: | `urls` | table | Links shown on PyPI (declared under `[project.urls]`) |
100: 
101: > **Note:** `authors` and `maintainers` also accept a plain string form (`authors = ["Your Name"]`), but the `{ name, email }` table form is recommended -- it is what published packages' `jac.toml` files use and what PyPI renders. See [`[project.include]`](#projectinclude) for controlling which files land in the wheel.
102: 
103: #### jac-version
104: 
105: `jac-version` records which Jac toolchain the project targets, written as a PEP 440-style specifier. Since the `jac` toolchain does not guarantee backward compatibility across versions (breaking changes ship as clean breaks), `jac create` stamps the **exact** version you created the project with:
106: 
107: ```toml
108: jac-version = "==0.34.3"
109: ```
110: 
111: You can widen or move it by editing the value -- `>=0.34.3`, `<=0.34.3`, `>=0.34,<0.35`, `~=0.34.3`, or a bare `0.34.3` (same as `==`).
112: 
113: At deploy time (`jac start --scale`), the pin selects the **pod runtime**: the deployer downloads the released `jac` binary, admin console, and base image from the release that satisfies `jac-version` and ships them to the pods, so the app runs on the toolchain it was built against -- not on whatever `latest` happens to be. Resolution rules:
114: 
115: - **Unset** -> the latest published release.
116: - **Exact pin** (`==X` / `X`) -> the `vX` release.
117: - **Range** -> the newest published release that satisfies it.
118: - **No published release satisfies the pin** (or the matching release lacks the pod's CPU arch or a `jac-*` asset) -> the deploy **aborts** with an error naming the pin; a pinned deploy never silently ships a different version. Fix or remove `jac-version` to proceed.
119: 
120: The pin is honored only on the default (stable) channel; the `[dev]`, `[experimental]`, and `JAC_SCALE_BINARY_PATH` (local) channels select the pod binary by their own rules and ignore it.
121: 
122: ---
123: 
124: ### [dependencies]
125: 
126: Python/PyPI packages:
127: 
128: ```toml
129: [dependencies]
130: requests = ">=2.28.0"
131: numpy = "1.24.0"
132: byllm = ">=0.4.8"
133: 
134: [dev-dependencies]
135: pytest = ">=8.0.0"
136: 
137: [dependencies.git]
138: my-lib = { git = "https://github.com/user/repo.git", branch = "main" }
139: 
140: [dependencies.system]
141: git = "*"
142: ffmpeg = "*"
143: ```
144: 
145: `[dependencies.system]` declares OS (apt) packages your app needs at runtime. On a `jac-scale` Kubernetes deploy they are installed into the service container at startup (Debian only; keys are apt package names). See [System Dependencies](../plugins/jac-scale-kubernetes.md#system-dependencies).
146: 
147: **Version specifiers:**
148: 
149: | Format | Example | Meaning |
150: |--------|---------|---------|
151: | Exact | `"1.0.0"` | Exactly 1.0.0 |
152: | Minimum | `">=1.0.0"` | 1.0.0 or higher |
153: | Range | `">=1.0,<2.0"` | 1.x only |
154: | Compatible | `"~=1.4.2"` | 1.4.x |
155: 
156: > **Default behavior:** When you run `jac install requests` without a version, the package is installed unconstrained and then the actual installed version is queried. A compatible-release spec (`~=X.Y`) is recorded -- e.g., if pip installs `2.32.5`, `jac.toml` gets `requests = "~=2.32"`. The `jac update` command also uses this format when writing updated versions back.

# Configuration Reference

The `jac.toml` file is the central configuration for Jac projects -- similar to `pyproject.toml` in Python or `package.json` in Node.js. It defines project metadata (name, version, entry point), manages dependencies (both PyPI and npm packages), sets defaults for CLI commands (test verbosity, server port, lint rules), configures built-in capabilities (LLM models, deployment targets), and supports environment-specific profiles (development vs. production).

You typically don't need to edit `jac.toml` manually for basic projects. The `jac create` command generates one with sensible defaults, and commands like `jac install <pkg>` and `jac config set` modify it for you. But understanding the full configuration surface is valuable when you need to customize build behavior, configure LLM providers, set up lint rules, or manage deployment settings.

`jac` commands locate `jac.toml` by walking up from the current working directory. The only exception is `jac install -e <path>`, which reads `jac.toml` from the resolved `<path>` so editable installs work from anywhere.

## Creating a Project

```bash
# Basic project
jac create myapp
cd myapp

# Full-stack web app (recommended for web development)

57: ## Configuration Sections
58: 
59: ### [project]
60: 
61: Project metadata. `entry-point` drives `jac run`. `jac-version` pins the Jac toolchain the project targets: `jac create` stamps it automatically, and `jac start --scale` uses it to select the pod runtime (see [jac-version](#jac-version) below). Publishing fields (`license`, `readme`, `keywords`, `requires-python`, `authors`, `maintainers`, and `[project.include]`) are used by `jac build --as wheel` when building a distributable wheel. All publishing fields are optional -- a project that is never published only needs `name`.
62: 
63: ```toml
64: [project]
65: name = "myapp"
66: version = "1.0.0"
67: description = "My Jac application"
68: entry-point = "main.jac"
69: kind = "service"   # drives `jac run` (omit to infer from the entry-point)
70: jac-version = "==0.34.3"   # stamped by `jac create`; widen to `>=`, `<=`, or a range
71: 
72: # Publishing metadata -- only needed to run `jac build --as wheel`
73: license = "MIT"
74: readme = "README.md"
75: requires-python = ">=3.12"
76: keywords = ["jac", "ai"]
77: authors = [{ name = "Your Name", email = "you@example.com" }]
78: maintainers = [{ name = "Another Person", email = "them@example.com" }]
79: 
80: [project.urls]
81: homepage = "https://example.com"
82: repository = "https://github.com/user/repo"
83: ```
84: 
85: | Field | Type | Description |
86: |-------|------|-------------|
87: | `name` | string | Project / PyPI package name (required) |
88: | `version` | string | Semantic version (default: `0.1.0`) |
89: | `description` | string | One-line summary (also shown on PyPI) |
90: | `entry-point` | string | Main file for `jac run` (default: `main.jac`) |
91: | `kind` | string | Project kind that drives `jac run` dispatch (execute / serve / build). Empty = inferred from the entry-point codespace. One of: `cli`, `cli-native`, `native-binary`, `native-lib`, `service`, `service-mesh`, `py-package`, `js-package`, `web-app`, `web-static`, `desktop`, `mobile` |
92: | `jac-version` | string | Jac toolchain version the project targets, as a PEP 440-style specifier. `jac create` stamps `==<current>`; at `jac start --scale` the pod runtime binary, admin console, and base image are all taken from the release that satisfies it, and the deploy aborts if none does. See [jac-version](#jac-version). |
93: | `license` | string | SPDX license identifier (e.g. `"MIT"`) |
94: | `readme` | string | Path to README file (default: `README.md`) |
95: | `requires-python` | string | Minimum Python version (e.g. `">=3.12"`) |
96: | `keywords` | list | Search keywords shown on PyPI |

98: | `maintainers` | list of `{name, email}` | Package maintainers |

100: 
101: > **Note:** `authors` and `maintainers` also accept a plain string form (`authors = ["Your Name"]`), but the `{ name, email }` table form is recommended -- it is what published packages' `jac.toml` files use and what PyPI renders. See [`[project.include]`](#projectinclude) for controlling which files land in the wheel.
102: 
103: #### jac-version
104: 
105: `jac-version` records which Jac toolchain the project targets, written as a PEP 440-style specifier. Since the `jac` toolchain does not guarantee backward compatibility across versions (breaking changes ship as clean breaks), `jac create` stamps the **exact** version you created the project with:
106: 
107: ```toml
108: jac-version = "==0.34.3"
109: ```
110: 
111: You can widen or move it by editing the value -- `>=0.34.3`, `<=0.34.3`, `>=0.34,<0.35`, `~=0.34.3`, or a bare `0.34.3` (same as `==`).
112: 
113: At deploy time (`jac start --scale`), the pin selects the **pod runtime**: the deployer downloads the released `jac` binary, admin console, and base image from the release that satisfies `jac-version` and ships them to the pods, so the app runs on the toolchain it was built against -- not on whatever `latest` happens to be. Resolution rules:
114: 
115: - **Unset** -> the latest published release.
116: - **Exact pin** (`==X` / `X`) -> the `vX` release.
117: - **Range** -> the newest published release that satisfies it.
118: - **No published release satisfies the pin** (or the matching release lacks the pod's CPU arch or a `jac-*` asset) -> the deploy **aborts** with an error naming the pin; a pinned deploy never silently ships a different version. Fix or remove `jac-version` to proceed.
119: 
120: The pin is honored only on the default (stable) channel; the `[dev]`, `[experimental]`, and `JAC_SCALE_BINARY_PATH` (local) channels select the pod binary by their own rules and ignore it.
121:

126: Python/PyPI packages:
127:

129: [dependencies]
130: requests = ">=2.28.0"
131: numpy = "1.24.0"
132: byllm = ">=0.4.8"

139: 
140: [dependencies.system]
141: git = "*"
142: ffmpeg = "*"
143: ```

145: `[dependencies.system]` declares OS (apt) packages your app needs at runtime. On a `jac-scale` Kubernetes deploy they are installed into the service container at startup (Debian only; keys are apt package names). See [System Dependencies](../plugins/jac-scale-kubernetes.md#system-dependencies).

147: **Version specifiers:**
148: 
149: | Format | Example | Meaning |
150: |--------|---------|---------|
151: | Exact | `"1.0.0"` | Exactly 1.0.0 |
152: | Minimum | `">=1.0.0"` | 1.0.0 or higher |
153: | Range | `">=1.0,<2.0"` | 1.x only |
154: | Compatible | `"~=1.4.2"` | 1.4.x |
155: 
156: > **Default behavior:** When you run `jac install requests` without a version, the package is installed unconstrained and then the actual installed version is queried. A compatible-release spec (`~=X.Y`) is recorded -- e.g., if pip installs `2.32.5`, `jac.toml` gets `requests = "~=2.32"`. The `jac update` command also uses this format when writing updated versions back.

## Goal

Build a small headless Jac document-intake backend for an eldercare assistant. A Patient graph node is the hub, and incoming Document nodes hang off it. Define Patient in graph/nodes/patient.jac and Document in graph/nodes/document.jac. Put the AI abilities in abilities/llm_abilities.jac: a module-level model named llm plus two LLM-backed functions, classify_document (returns one document category name such as EOB, MEDICAL_BILL or WILL) and translate_to_plain_english (returns a plain-English summary for an elderly reader). Add two walkers that start at a Patient and visit its documents: DocumentClassify in graph/walkers/intake/document_classify.jac stores the category on documents still marked UNKNOWN, and PlainEnglishTranslator in graph/walkers/intake/plain_english_translator.jac stores a summary on documents that have content but no summary yet. Either walker stops its whole walk at the first document it should skip. A thin main.jac imports everything. Include tests that replace the model with MockLLM.

## Module relationships

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M1["graph/nodes/patient.jac"]
    M2["graph/nodes/document.jac"]
    M3["abilities/llm_abilities.jac"]
    M4["graph/walkers/intake/document_classify.jac"]
    M5["graph/walkers/intake/plain_english_translator.jac"]
    M6["main.jac"]
    M1 --> M4
    M2 --> M4
    M3 --> M4
    M1 --> M5
    M2 --> M5
    M3 --> M5
    M1 --> M6
    M2 --> M6
    M3 --> M6
    M4 --> M6
    M5 --> M6
```

An arrow points from a provider to a module that imports it.

## Frontend modules (.jac)


## Backend modules (.jac)

- `graph/nodes/patient.jac` — Define node Patient, the hub of the graph, with required name:str and str fields defaulting to "": dob, medicare_id, medicaid_id, address, city, state, zip_code, phone, email, emergency_contact_name, emergency_contact_phone, created_at, updated_at, plus primary_language:str default "English". No abilities. Public interface: `Patient`.
- `graph/nodes/document.jac` — Define node Document for a raw incoming document. Every field has a default so Document(...) can be built with keywords only: doc_id, doc_type, title, raw_content, raw_text, source, original_filename, mime_type, ingested_at, plain_english_summary, embedding_id, content_hash are str default ""; source_channel:str default "email"; classification:str default "UNKNOWN" (the sentinel for not yet classified); processed:bool default False. No abilities. Public interface: `Document`.
- `abilities/llm_abilities.jac` — Import environ from os and Model from jaclang.byllm.lib. Declare glob llm = Model(model_name="openrouter/anthropic/claude-4.6-sonnet", api_key=environ.get("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", "")). Declare two body-less LLM functions delegated with by llm(model=llm) and described by sem strings: classify_document returns ONLY one category name from EOB, MSN_PART_A, MSN_PART_B, MEDICAL_BILL, CMS1500_CLAIM, UB04_CLAIM, INSURANCE_NOTICE, POLICY_CHANGE, HIPAA_AUTH, POWER_OF_ATTORNEY, WILL, TRUST, BENEFICIARY_FORM, LEGAL_NOTICE, FINANCIAL_STATEMENT, APPOINTMENT_CONFIRMATION, PRESCRIPTION_NOTICE, SCAM_COMMUNICATION, UNKNOWN; translate_to_plain_english rewrites technical medical billing or legal content at about a 6th-grade reading level for a 75-year-old reader, ending with a one-sentence 'Bottom line:' summary. The module-level name must be exactly llm so tests can replace it with MockLLM; the returned string is used as-is by callers. Public interface: `llm`, `classify_document`, `translate_to_plain_english`.
- `graph/walkers/intake/document_classify.jac` — Import Patient from graph.nodes.patient, Document from graph.nodes.document and classify_document from abilities.llm_abilities (absolute imports). walker DocumentClassify has no fields. On Patient entry it visits all outgoing neighbours ([-->]), in connection order. On Document entry: if here.classification != "UNKNOWN" it executes disengage, which ends the ENTIRE walk (later documents are not visited and no model call is made). Otherwise it builds source_meta = {"source": here.source, "filename": here.original_filename, "mime_type": here.mime_type}, calls classify_document(raw_text=here.raw_content, source_metadata=source_meta), assigns the returned string unchanged to here.classification, and prints "[DocumentClassify] Document <doc_id> classified as: <category>". It reports nothing. Public interface: `DocumentClassify`.
- `graph/walkers/intake/plain_english_translator.jac` — Import Patient from graph.nodes.patient, Document from graph.nodes.document and translate_to_plain_english from abilities.llm_abilities (absolute imports). walker PlainEnglishTranslator has no fields. On Patient entry it visits [-->] in connection order. On Document entry: if here.plain_english_summary != "" or here.raw_content == "" it executes disengage, ending the ENTIRE walk (later documents keep their summary unchanged and no model call is made). Otherwise it calls translate_to_plain_english(technical_content=here.raw_content[:4000], content_type=here.classification, reading_level=6), stores the returned string unchanged in here.plain_english_summary (classification is not modified), and prints "[PlainEnglishTranslator] Translated doc <doc_id> (<classification>)". It reports nothing. Public interface: `PlainEnglishTranslator`.
- `main.jac` — Thin entry module holding only imports: Patient, Document, classify_document, translate_to_plain_english, DocumentClassify and PlainEnglishTranslator from their modules (graph.nodes.patient, graph.nodes.document, abilities.llm_abilities, graph.walkers.intake.document_classify, graph.walkers.intake.plain_english_translator). No other code. Public interface: —.

## Backend modules (.jac)

- `server/config.jac` — Hard-rule constants enforced in code, declared as one glob statement: INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP:int = 20, MAX_DAILY_HOURS:int = 8 (students), MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER:int = 12, WORKER_WEEKLY_LIMIT:int = 60, MIN_REST_MINUTES:int = 30. No imports. Public interface: `INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP`, `MAX_DAILY_HOURS`, `MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER`, `WORKER_WEEKLY_LIMIT`, `MIN_REST_MINUTES`.
- `server/timeutil.jac` — Time helpers; times are minutes from midnight, days 0=Mon..6=Sun. Imports date, timedelta from datetime only. glob DAY_SHORT = ["Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat","Sun"] and DAY_LONG = full day names Monday..Sunday. hm(minutes) -> zero-padded "HH:MM". parse_hm(text) -> minutes from "H:MM" (strips text; missing/empty minute part counts as 0). slot_label(day,start,end) -> f"{DAY_SHORT[day]} {hm(start)}–{hm(end)}" (en dash). hours(start,end) -> (end-start)/60. overlaps(a_start,a_end,b_start,b_end) -> a_start < b_end and b_start < a_end (touching intervals do not overlap). monday_of(d) -> d minus d.weekday() days. week_key(d, dflt) -> dflt.isoformat() when d is empty, else the ISO Monday of date d. fmt_hours(h) -> integer text when h is whole, else one decimal. g(v) -> f"{v:g}". plural(n, word, many="") -> word when n == 1 else (many or word + "s"). {"file_path": "/workspace/docs/plan.md", "content": "# Implementation plan

## Goal

Build the headless shift-rule core of CampusSync, a scheduler for student and worker shift jobs. server/config.jac holds the hard-rule constants. server/timeutil.jac holds time helpers (times are minutes from midnight, days 0=Mon..6=Sun), including an interval overlap test. server/models.jac defines the graph nodes Employer, Employee, BusyBlock, Employment and Shift, plus the lookups employer_of, employee_of and held_shifts. server/rules.jac builds the in-memory Ledger for one week. Ledger.check returns a Verdict with an internal code, a public reason, the hours the employer may still schedule, and whether another employer is involved. The Ledger also supports clone, in-memory add/remove of held shifts, hour totals and a whole-week violations list. main.jac imports and re-exports the public names. Target: Jac 0.36.1, backend-only. Jac 0.36.1 infers placement, so there are no cl/sv markers.

## Module relationships

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M1["server/config.jac"]
    M2["server/timeutil.jac"]
    M3["server/models.jac"]
    M4["server/rules.jac"]
    M5["main.jac"]
    M1 --> M3
    M1 --> M4
    M2 --> M4
    M3 --> M4
    M3 --> M5
    M4 --> M5
```

An arrow points from a provider to the module that imports it.

## Frontend modules (.jac)

None. This is a headless service with no JSX or browser UI.

## Backend modules (.jac)

- `server/config.jac`
  - One glob statement: INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP:int = 20, MAX_DAILY_HOURS:int = 8, MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER:int = 12, WORKER_WEEKLY_LIMIT:int = 60, MIN_REST_MINUTES:int = 30.
  - No imports.
  - Public interface: `INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP`, `MAX_DAILY_HOURS`, `MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER`, `WORKER_WEEKLY_LIMIT`, `MIN_REST_MINUTES`.
- `server/timeutil.jac`
  - Imports date and timedelta from datetime only.
  - Globals: DAY_SHORT (Mon..Sun) and DAY_LONG (Monday..Sunday).
  - Helpers:
    - hm: zero-padded "HH:MM".
    - parse_hm: strips the text; a missing or empty minute part counts as 0.
    - slot_label: "Day HH:MM–HH:MM" with an en dash.
    - hours: (end - start) / 60.
    - overlaps: a_start < b_end and b_start < a_end. Touching intervals do not overlap.
    - monday_of: d minus d.weekday() days.
    - week_key: dflt.isoformat() when d is empty, otherwise the ISO Monday of date d.
    - fmt_hours: integer text when h is whole, otherwise one decimal.
    - g: f"{v:g}".
    - plural: word when n == 1, otherwise many or word + "s".
  - Public interface: `DAY_SHORT`, `DAY_LONG`, `hm`, `parse_hm`, `slot_label`, `hours`, `overlaps`, `monday_of`, `week_key`, `fmt_hours`, `g`, `plural`.
- `server/models.jac`
  - Graph nodes. Records reference each other by jid strings.
  - Imports INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP, MAX_DAILY_HOURS and MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER from server.config.
  - Employee methods:
    - first_name: the first space-separated word of name.
    - is_international: kind == "student" and status == "international".
    - cap: min(weekly_limit or 20, 20) when international, otherwise weekly_limit.
    - daily_max: 8 for students, 12 for workers.
  - Shift.hours: (end - start) / 60.
  - employer_of and employee_of: None for an empty id; otherwise jobj(id) if it is that node type, else None.
  - held_shifts(s, wk, want): the Shift nodes linked from employee s with week == wk and status == want.
  - Public interface: `Employer`, `Employee`, `BusyBlock`, `Employment`, `Shift`, `employer_of`, `employee_of`, `held_shifts`.
- `server/rules.jac`
  - Deterministic conflict agent and compliance checker.
  - Imports MIN_REST_MINUTES from server.config, overlaps from server.timeutil, and Employee, BusyBlock, Employment, Shift and employee_of from server.models.
  - Globals: CONFLICT = "schedule_conflict", HOUR_LIMIT = "hour_limit", NOT_ON_TEAM = "not_on_team", NOT_QUALIFIED = "not_qualified", _TIMING = [overlap, rest, daily_max], _HOURS = [weekly_cap, dept_hours].
  - Objects: Held, Block, Verdict and Ledger (caches keyed by sid or by sid|did).
  - Ledger.check order:
    1. No allotment gives not_on_team.
    2. Not qualified gives not_qualified.
    3. A failed conflict verdict is returned with hours_left set to hours_left(sid, did).
    4. Otherwise the result of compliance.

# Configuration Reference

The `jac.toml` file is the central configuration for Jac projects -- similar to `pyproject.toml` in Python or `package.json` in Node.js. It defines project metadata (name, version, entry point), manages dependencies (both PyPI and npm packages), sets defaults for CLI commands (test verbosity, server port, lint rules), configures built-in capabilities (LLM models, deployment targets), and supports environment-specific profiles (development vs. production).

You typically don't need to edit `jac.toml` manually for basic projects. The `jac create` command generates one with sensible defaults, and commands like `jac install <pkg>` and `jac config set` modify it for you. But understanding the full configuration surface is valuable when you need to customize build behavior, configure LLM providers, set up lint rules, or manage deployment settings.

`jac` commands locate `jac.toml` by walking up from the current working directory. The only exception is `jac install -e <path>`, which reads `jac.toml` from the resolved `<path>` so editable installs work from anywhere.

## Creating a Project

```bash
# Basic project
jac create myapp
cd myapp

# Full-stack web app (recommended for web development)
jac create myapp --kind web-static
cd myapp
```

This creates a `jac.toml` with default settings. When using `--kind web-static`, the scaffolded project includes:

```
myapp/
├── main.jac                  # Entry point with the client app

... (899 lines omitted) ...


### Scale: Webhooks

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Secret for webhook HMAC signatures |
| `WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_HEADER` | Header name for signature |
| `WEBHOOK_VERIFY_SIGNATURE` | Enable signature verification |
| `WEBHOOK_API_KEY_EXPIRY_DAYS` | API key expiry in days |

### Scale: Kubernetes

Deployment settings (app name, namespace, node port, CPU/memory requests and limits, health probes) are configured in `jac.toml` under `[scale.kubernetes]` -- see the [Kubernetes reference](../plugins/jac-scale-kubernetes.md). At deploy time, jac-scale injects these variables into every pod:

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `K8S_APP_NAME` | Application name (used by observability and admin tooling inside the pod) |
| `K8S_NAMESPACE` | Namespace the workload runs in |

---

## See Also

- [CLI Reference](../cli/index.md) - Command-line interface documentation
- [Publishing Packages](../publishing.md) - Building and uploading wheels to PyPI

## Goal

Build the headless scoring core of Flair, a retention/engagement auditor for consumer web apps. A crawler (out of scope) produces deterministic signals; an LLM rubric evaluator turns an evidence pack plus those signals into a JSON text verdict, and the service parses that verdict into a typed audit bundle with clamped category scores and normalized findings. When the LLM call fails, returns unparsable text, or gives no findings, the service must fall back to a bundle built from the deterministic retention signals. Put the plain data objects DeterministicSignal, LlmFindingDraft and LlmAuditBundle in services/models.jac; the by-llm rubric function evaluate_retention_recommendations and its module-level model glob llm in services/llm.jac; and the parsing, clamping, fallback and weighted-rubric logic (safe_retention_bundle, parse_llm_bundle, fallback_bundle, rubric_overall, blended_score and their helpers) in services/audits.jac. main.jac only imports the public audit functions. Include tests that swap the model for MockLLM.

## Module relationships

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M1["services/models.jac"]
    M2["services/llm.jac"]
    M3["services/audits.jac"]
    M4["main.jac"]
    M1 --> M2
    M1 --> M3
    M2 --> M3
    M3 --> M4
```

An arrow points from a provider to a module that imports it.

## Frontend modules (.jac)


## Backend modules (.jac)

- `services/models.jac` — Plain obj declarations (no nodes, no imports), each field with a default. obj DeterministicSignal has lane_retention_or_conversion:str="", category:str="", severity:str="medium", confidence:float=0.7, page_url:str="", issue_location:str="", evidence_ref:str="", evidence:str="", proof:str="", why_it_matters:str="", research_basis:str="", recommendation:str="", fix_guidance:str="", exact_ui_or_copy_tip:str="", primary_metric:str="", guardrail_metric:str="", estimated_effort:str="medium", expected_impact:str="medium". obj LlmFindingDraft has category:str="", lane_retention_or_conversion:str="", severity:str="medium", confidence:float=0.7, then the same string fields as DeterministicSignal from page_url through expected_impact with the same defaults, plus legal_safe:bool=True. obj LlmAuditBundle has score:int=60, the ten int category scores onboarding_activation, habit_loop_strength, reward_design_feedback, social_retention_mechanics, attention_capture_session_depth, personalization_adaptation, friction_reduction, progression_investment, reentry_notification_systems, trust_emotional_safety each default 5, strengths, weaknesses, retention_risks, highest_leverage_improvements as list[str] default [], dark_pattern_risk_score:int=0, dark_pattern_risk_reasons:list[str]=[], findings:list[LlmFindingDraft]=[]. Every obj and field carries a short sem description of its meaning for the LLM. Public interface: `DeterministicSignal`, `LlmFindingDraft`, `LlmAuditBundle`.
- `services/llm.jac` — Import Model from jaclang.byllm.lib and DeterministicSignal, LlmAuditBundle, LlmFindingDraft from services/models.jac. Declare glob llm: Model = Model(model_name="gpt-4o"). Declare the body-less function evaluate_retention_recommendations(target_url, evidence_pack, deterministic_signals: list[DeterministicSignal]) -> str by llm(max_tokens=3600), with the function sem and the three parameter sems exactly as given in signatures. The function returns raw JSON text; it never parses anything itself. Public interface: `llm`, `evaluate_retention_recommendations`.
- `services/audits.jac` — Import traceback and json; import DeterministicSignal, LlmFindingDraft, LlmAuditBundle from services/models.jac and evaluate_retention_recommendations from services/llm.jac. bounded_score clamps an int to 0..100; bounded_ten clamps to 0..10; blended_score(a,b) = bounded_score((bounded_score(a) + bounded_score(b)) // 2). rubric_overall(bundle): weighted float sum of bounded_ten of each category times its weight: onboarding_activation 1.0, habit_loop_strength 1.2, reward_design_feedback 1.1, social_retention_mechanics 1.0, attention_capture_session_depth 1.1, personalization_adaptation 1.2, friction_reduction 1.1, progression_investment 1.2, reentry_notification_systems 1.0, trust_emotional_safety 0.9; return bounded_score(int((weighted / 10.8) * 10.0)). draft_from_signal(signal) copies the 18 shared fields (lane_retention_or_conversion, category, severity, confidence, page_url, issue_location, evidence_ref, evidence, proof, why_it_matters, research_basis, recommendation, fix_guidance, exact_ui_or_copy_tip, primary_metric, guardrail_metric, estimated_effort, expected_impact) into an LlmFindingDraft with legal_safe=True. fallback_bundle(lane, signals, score): findings = draft_from_signal of every signal whose lane_retention_or_conversion == lane, in input order; if none, one baseline LlmFindingDraft with category "baseline opportunity", the given lane, severity "medium", confidence 0.55, page_url "", estimated_effort "low", expected_impact "medium", primary_metric lane + " score", guardrail_metric "support tickets and complaint rate", legal_safe True and short cautious explanatory text in the remaining fields. category_score is 5, but 3 when score < 40 and 7 when score > 75; all ten categories get category_score; bundle score = score unchanged; strengths []; weaknesses, retention_risks and highest_leverage_improvements each exactly one explanatory sentence (weaknesses says the LLM rubric evaluation was unavailable so deterministic crawler signals were used); dark_pattern_risk_score 0; dark_pattern_risk_reasons []. llm_json_payload(text): strip; drop a leading ```json (else a leading ```) and a trailing ```, stripping again; then if a '{' exists and the last '}' is at or after it, return the substring from the first '{' through the last '}' inclusive, else the cleaned text. json_str(data,key,fallback) returns str(data[key]) unless that is "None" or access fails (then fallback); json_int/json_float/json_bool cast data[key] with int/float/bool, fallback on any exception; json_string_list returns [str(item) for item in data[key]], returning the items collected so far on exception. bounded_confidence clamps a float to 0.0..1.0. parse_llm_findings(data) builds one LlmFindingDraft per item of data["findings"]: lane_retention_or_conversion always "retention"; {"file_path": "/workspace/docs/plan.md", "content": "# Flair backend: implementation plan

## Goal

Build the headless scoring core of Flair, a retention and engagement auditor for consumer web apps. A crawler (out of scope) produces deterministic signals. An LLM rubric evaluator turns an evidence pack plus those signals into a JSON text verdict. The service parses that verdict into a typed audit bundle with clamped category scores and normalized findings.

The service falls back to a bundle built from the deterministic retention signals in three cases:

- the LLM call fails
- the LLM returns text that cannot be parsed
- the LLM returns no findings

Target: Jac 0.36.1, backend only (no JSX, no browser UI). Placement is inferred, so files use no `cl`/`sv` markers. Tests never call a real model; they use MockLLM.

## Module relationships

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M1["services/models.jac"]
    M2["services/llm.jac"]
    M3["services/audits.jac"]
    M4["main.jac"]
    M1 --> M2
    M1 --> M3
    M2 --> M3
    M3 --> M4
```

An arrow points from a provider to the module that imports it.

## Frontend modules (.jac)

None. This is a headless service slice.

## Backend modules (.jac)

- `services/models.jac`: plain `obj` declarations with no imports. Every field has a default, and every obj and field has a sem description.
- `services/llm.jac`: holds `glob llm: Model` and the body-less function `evaluate_retention_recommendations ... by llm(max_tokens=3600)`, along with its function and parameter sems.
- `services/audits.jac`: clamping, the weighted rubric, the JSON payload extractor, safe JSON accessors, finding parsing, bundle parsing, the fallback bundle, and the safe orchestration entry.
- `main.jac`: one import of the public audit functions and no declarations of its own.

## Public interfaces

### services/models.jac

- `obj DeterministicSignal`:
  - `lane_retention_or_conversion`, `category`: str, default `""`
  - `severity`: str, default `"medium"`
  - `confidence`: float, default `0.7`
  - `page_url`, `issue_location`, `evidence_ref`, `evidence`, `proof`, `why_it_matters`, `research_basis`, `recommendation`, `fix_guidance`, `exact_ui_or_copy_tip`, `primary_metric`, `guardrail_metric`: str, default `""`
  - `estimated_effort`, `expected_impact`: str, default `"medium"`
- `obj LlmFindingDraft`:
  - `category`, `lane_retention_or_conversion`: str, default `""`
  - `severity`: str, default `"medium"`
  - `confidence`: float, default `0.7`
  - the same string fields as DeterministicSignal, from `page_url` through `expected_impact`, with the same defaults
  - `legal_safe`: bool, default `True`
- `obj LlmAuditBundle`:
  - `score`: int, default `60`
  - ten int category scores, each default `5`: `onboarding_activation`, `habit_loop_strength`, `reward_design_feedback`, `social_retention_mechanics`, `attention_capture_session_depth`, `personalization_adaptation`, `friction_reduction`, `progression_investment`, `reentry_notification_systems`, `trust_emotional_safety`
  - `strengths`, `weaknesses`, `retention_risks`, `highest_leverage_improvements`: list[str], default `[]`
  - `dark_pattern_risk_score`: int, default `0`
  - `dark_pattern_risk_reasons`: list[str], default `[]`
  - `findings`: list[LlmFindingDraft], default `[]`

### services/llm.jac

- `glob llm: Model = Model(model_name="gpt-4o");`
  - `Model` is imported from `jaclang.byllm.lib`.
- `def evaluate_retention_recommendations(target_url: str, evidence_pack: str, deterministic_signals: list[DeterministicSignal]) -> str by llm(max_tokens=3600);`
  - The function and its three parameters carry their sems verbatim from the task.
  - It reads the module-level `llm` at call time, so tests can swap in MockLLM.

### services/audits.jac

| Signature | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `def bounded_score(score: int) -> int` | Clamps to 0..100. |
| `def bounded_ten(score: int) -> int` | Clamps to 0..10. |
| `def blended_score(llm_score: int, deterministic_score: int) -> int` | Returns `bounded_score((bounded_score(a) + bounded_score(b)) // 2)`. |
| `def rubric_overall(bundle: LlmAuditBundle) -> int` | Weighted sum of the ten `bounded_ten` category scores, then `bounded_score(int((w / 10.8) * 10.0))`. |
| `def draft_from_signal(signal: DeterministicSignal) -> LlmFindingDraft` | Copies the 18 shared fields and sets `legal_safe=True`. |
| `def fallback_bundle(lane: str, signals: list[DeterministicSignal], score: int) -> LlmAuditBundle` | Builds the deterministic fallback bundle described below. |
| `def llm_json_payload(text: str) -> str` | Strips code fences and surrounding prose; returns the span from the first `{` to the last `}`. |
| `def json_str(data: any, key: str, fallback_value: str) -> str` | Safe accessor; falls back if the key is missing or the value is `"None"`. |
| `def json_int(data: any, key: str, fallback_value: int) -> int` | Safe accessor. |
| `def json_float(data: any, key: str, fallback_value: float) -> float` | Safe accessor. |
| `def json_bool(data: any, key: str, fallback_value: bool) -> bool` | Safe accessor. |
| `def json_string_list(data: any, key: str) -> list[str]` | Safe accessor; returns the items collected before any error. |
| `def bounded_confidence(value: float) -> float` | Clamps to 0.0..1.0. |
| `def parse_llm_findings(data: any) -> list[LlmFindingDraft]` | Parses findings as described below. |
| `def parse_llm_bundle(result: str, signals: list[DeterministicSignal], score: int) -> LlmAuditBundle` | Parses the model text as described below. |
| `def safe_retention_bundle(target_url: str, evidence_pack: str, signals: list[DeterministicSignal], score: int) -> LlmAuditBundle` | Calls the evaluator, parses the result, and falls back on any exception. |

Rubric weights used by `rubric_overall`:

| Category | Weight |
| --- | ---: |
| onboarding_activation | 1.0 |
| habit_loop_strength | 1.2 |
| reward_design_feedback | 1.1 |
| social_retention_mechanics | 1.0 |
| attention_capture_session_depth | 1.1 |
| personalization_adaptation | 1.2 |
| friction_reduction | 1.1 |
| progression_investment | 1.2 |
| reentry_notification_systems | 1.0 |
| trust_emotional_safety | 0.9 |

`fallback_bundle` behavior:

- Findings are `draft_from_signal` of each signal whose lane matches, in input order.
- If no signal matches, it uses one baseline finding:
  - category "baseline opportunity", severity "medium", confidence 0.55
  - estimated_effort "low", expected_impact "medium"
  - primary_metric is the lane followed by " score"
  - guardrail_metric "support tickets and complaint rate"
- Every category gets a value of 3 if the score is below 40, 7 if the score is above 75, and 5 otherwise.
- The bundle score is the given score, unchanged.
- `weaknesses`, `retention_risks` and `highest_leverage_improvements` each hold one sentence.

`parse_llm_findings` behavior:

- Every finding is forced into the `"retention"` lane.
- Defaults:
  - category "retention loop", severity "medium"
  - confidence 0.7, clamped
  - primary_metric "repeat sessions", guardrail_metric "complaints and opt-outs"
  - estimated_effort "medium", expected_impact "medium"
  - legal_safe True
  - all other string fields ""
- If an error occurs, it returns the findings parsed so far.

`parse_llm_bundle` behavior:

- It runs `json.loads` on the result of `llm_json_payload`. Parse errors propagate to the caller.
- If no findings are parsed, it returns `fallback_bundle("retention", signals, score)`.
- Otherwise the score is clamped to 0..100, each category is clamped to 0..10 with default 5, and the list fields are read with `json_string_list`.
- `dark_pattern_risk_score` is `bounded_ten`, with default 0.

## Goal

Build the headless backend of a health-insurance appeal agent. In models.jac define the denial-reason and appeal-strength enums, the value objects PolicyClause, Contradiction and AppealLetter, and graph nodes Claim, Policy and Appeal. In tools.jac define five LLM-backed tools: classify the denial reason, extract the relevant policy clauses, find contradictions between the denial and the policy, assess appeal strength, and draft the appeal letter. Each tool asks the model for plain text or JSON text and converts the answer into the typed model objects in Jac, tolerating markdown fences and surrounding prose. In walkers.jac expose a public walker submit_claim that stores the claim and policy on root, runs the five tools in sequence, stores an Appeal node and reports the letter, and a public walker list_appeals that reports a summary row per stored appeal. main.jac only imports the two walkers. ## Module relationships

```mermaid

    M2["tools.jac"]
    M3["walkers.jac"]

## Backend modules (.jac)

Value objects PolicyClause(section, title, text, relevance_note default ""), Contradiction(denial_quote, policy_quote, clause_section, explanation) and AppealLetter(subject, salutation, body, citations: list[str], closing). Persistent nodes Claim (claim_id, patient_name, member_id, cpt_code, date_of_service, billed_amount: float, denial_text, clinical_record default ""), Policy (policy_id, plan_name, full_text) and Appeal (appeal_id, claim_id, policy_id, denial_reason: DenialReason, strength: AppealStrength, contradictions_json: str holding a serialized list of contradiction dicts, letter_subject, letter_body, citations_json: str holding a serialized list of citation strings, created_at: str). Public interface: `DenialReason`, `AppealStrength`, `PolicyClause`, `Contradiction`, `AppealLetter`, `Claim`, `Policy`, `Appeal`.
- `tools.jac` — Imports os, json, re, Model from jaclang.byllm.llm, and DenialReason, PolicyClause, Contradiction, AppealLetter, AppealStrength from models.jac. _pick_model() returns a Model chosen from environment variables in this order: FEATHERLESS_API_KEY -> Model(model_name=APPEAL_MODEL env or "openai/Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct", api_key=that key); ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -> "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"; GEMINI_API_KEY -> "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash"; OPENAI_API_KEY -> "gpt-4o-mini"; otherwise raise Exception naming the four variables. {"file_path": "/workspace/docs/plan.md", "content": "# InsuraAgent backend: implementation plan

Target: Jac 0.36.1. Backend-only service. No JSX and no browser UI. Placement is inferred, so files use no `cl`/`sv` markers. Tests never call a real model; they use MockLLM.

## Goal

Build a headless health-insurance appeal agent.

- `models.jac` holds the typed data model.
- `tools.jac` holds five LLM-backed tools. Each tool asks the model for plain text or JSON text, then parses the answer into typed objects. Parsing tolerates markdown fences and surrounding prose.
- `walkers.jac` exposes two public walkers:
  - `submit_claim` stores the claim and policy, runs the five tools in sequence, stores an Appeal, and reports the letter.
  - `list_appeals` reports one summary row per stored appeal.
- `main.jac` only re-exports the two walkers.

## Module relationships

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M1["models.jac"]
    M2["tools.jac"]
    M3["walkers.jac"]
    M4["main.jac"]
    M1 --> M2
    M1 --> M3
    M2 --> M3
    M3 --> M4
```

Each arrow points from a provider to the module that imports it.

## Frontend modules (.jac)

None. This is a backend-only service.

## Backend modules (.jac)

- `models.jac`
  - Imports: none.
  - Public interface: `DenialReason`, `AppealStrength`, `PolicyClause`, `Contradiction`, `AppealLetter`, `Claim`, `Policy`, `Appeal`.
- `tools.jac`
  - Imports: `os`, `json`, `re`, `Model` from `jaclang.byllm.llm`, and models.
  - Public interface: `llm`, `extract_denial_reason`, `extract_relevant_clauses`, `find_contradictions`, `assess_appeal_strength`, `draft_appeal_letter`.
- `walkers.jac`
  - Imports: `json`, `uuid`, `datetime`, models, and tools.
  - Public interface: `submit_claim`, `list_appeals`.
- `main.jac`
  - Contents: only `import from walkers { submit_claim, list_appeals }`.
  - Public interface: `submit_claim`, `list_appeals`.

## Public signatures

### models.jac

- `enum DenialReason { NOT_MEDICALLY_NECESSARY, OUT_OF_NETWORK, PRIOR_AUTH_MISSING, EXPERIMENTAL_OR_INVESTIGATIONAL, CODING_ERROR, BENEFIT_EXCLUSION, OTHER }`
- `enum AppealStrength { WEAK, MODERATE, STRONG, VERY_STRONG }`
- `obj PolicyClause { section: str, title: str, text: str, relevance_note: str = "" }`
- `obj Contradiction { denial_quote: str, policy_quote: str, clause_section: str, explanation: str }`
- `obj AppealLetter { subject: str, salutation: str, body: str, citations: list[str], closing: str }`
- `node Claim { claim_id, patient_name, member_id, cpt_code, date_of_service: str, billed_amount: float, denial_text: str, clinical_record: str = "" }`
- `node Policy { policy_id, plan_name, full_text: str }`
- `node Appeal { appeal_id, claim_id, policy_id: str, denial_reason: DenialReason, strength: AppealStrength, contradictions_json, letter_subject, letter_body, citations_json, created_at: str }`

### tools.jac

Helpers and the model glob:

- `def _pick_model() -> Model`
  - Checks environment keys in this order: FEATHERLESS (uses APPEAL_MODEL, or `openai/Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct`), then ANTHROPIC, then GEMINI, then OPENAI.
  - If none is set, it raises an exception.
- `glob llm = _pick_model();`
- `def _parse_json_obj(s: str) -> dict`
- `def _parse_json_list(s: str) -> list`

Raw `by llm()` functions. Each returns `str` and has a docstring prompt:

- `extract_denial_reason_raw(denial_text)`
- `extract_relevant_clauses_raw(policy_text, denial_reason)`
- `find_contradictions_raw(denial_text, clinical_record, clauses)`
- `assess_appeal_strength_raw(contradictions)`
- `draft_appeal_letter_raw(...)`, which takes 10 arguments.

Public tools. Each makes exactly one model call:

- `extract_denial_reason(denial_text: str) -> DenialReason`
- `extract_relevant_clauses(policy_text: str, denial_reason: DenialReason) -> list[PolicyClause]`
- `find_contradictions(denial_text: str, clinical_record: str, clauses: list[PolicyClause]) -> list[Contradiction]`
- `assess_appeal_strength(contradictions: list[Contradiction]) -> AppealStrength`
- `draft_appeal_letter(patient_name, member_id, claim_number, date_of_service, cpt_code, billed_amount: float, plan_name, denial_reason: DenialReason, contradictions: list[Contradiction], clinical_record) -> AppealLetter`

### walkers.jac

- `walker:pub submit_claim`
  - Fields: `patient_name`, `member_id`, `claim_number`, `date_of_service`, `cpt_code`, `billed_amount: float`, `plan_name`, `denial_text`, `policy_text`, `clinical_record = ""`.
  - Ability: `can run with Root entry`.
- `walker:pub list_appeals`
  - Ability: `can run with Root entry`.

## Behavior rules

### Mapping model answers to enums

The raw answer is uppercased and stripped. The first matching substring rule wins.

`extract_denial_reason`:

| Substring in answer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `NOT_MEDICALLY_NECESSARY` | NOT_MEDICALLY_NECESSARY |
| `OUT_OF_NETWORK` | OUT_OF_NETWORK |
| `PRIOR_AUTH` | PRIOR_AUTH_MISSING |
| `EXPERIMENTAL` or `INVESTIGATIONAL` | EXPERIMENTAL_OR_INVESTIGATIONAL |
| `CODING` | CODING_ERROR |
| `EXCLUSION` | BENEFIT_EXCLUSION |
| anything else | OTHER |

`assess_appeal_strength`:

| Substring in answer | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `VERY_STRONG` or `VERY STRONG` | VERY_STRONG |
| `STRONG` | STRONG |
| `WEAK` | WEAK |
| anything else | MODERATE |

### Parsing JSON answers

`_parse_json_obj` and `_parse_json_list` work the same way:

1. Strip the text.
2. If a ```` ```json ```` or ```` ``` ```` fence wraps the value, use the fenced content.
3. Otherwise, take the span from the first opening bracket to its matching closing bracket, found by counting depth.
4. Parse it with `json.loads`.
5. On any failure, return `{}` or `[]`.

List tools skip elements that are not dicts. Missing fields become `str(d.get(k, ""))`.

In `draft_appeal_letter`:

- `citations` defaults to `[]`.
- A non-list `citations` value is wrapped as `[str(x)]`.

### What submit_claim stores and reports

- Policy ID: `POL-{member_id}`.
- Appeal ID: `APL-{uuid4().hex[:8]}`.
- `letter_body` is `salutation + "\n\n" + body + "\n\n" + closing`.
- Report: `{appeal_id, claim_id, subject, letter, citations}`.

`list_appeals` reports ONE list of rows. Each row is `{appeal_id, claim_id, subject, created_at}`.

## Scaffold write order

1. `docs/plan.md`
2. `jac.toml`, the support file: `[project]` with name `insuraagent-backend`, kind `service`, entry-point `main.jac`.
3. `models.jac`
4. `tools.jac`, with stub bodies.
5. `walkers.jac`, with stub bodies.
6. `main.jac`
7. Tests: `tests/test_tools.jac` and `tests/test_walkers.jac`.

## Verification

1. Run `jac check` on each module and on `main.jac`.
2. Run `jac test`. Tests set `OPENAI_API_KEY` to a placeholder before importing tools, then set `tools.llm = MockLLM(...)`. Outputs are given in call order: reason, clauses JSON, contradictions JSON, strength, letter JSON.
3. Flow check: `submit_claim` attaches Claim, Policy and Appeal to root, then `list_appeals` reports one row per appeal.
"}

In services/supply_agent.jac implement the supply_manager walker: spawned on a BusinessNode with a food type, quantity and ISO expiry time, it rejects food that is already expired with an error report, and otherwise creates a pending DonationNode, links it from the business with an Offers edge, anchors it to root, remembers it on the walker and reports a summary. main.jac only imports the model and the walker. Empty typed edges: Offers (BusinessNode -> DonationNode), AllocatedTo (DonationNode -> ShelterNode), AssignedVolunteer (DonationNode -> VolunteerNode), ConnectedToHub (domain node -> HubNode). Public interface: `HubNode`, `BusinessNode`, `ShelterNode`, `DonationNode`, `VolunteerNode`, `Offers`, `AllocatedTo`, `AssignedVolunteer`, `ConnectedToHub`.
- `services/supply_agent.jac` — Imports datetime from datetime and BusinessNode, DonationNode, Offers from services.nourish_model (absolute import path). walker supply_manager has payload food_type: str, quantity: int, expiry_time: str (zero-padded ISO-8601 like 2025-12-31T18:00:00) and result fields created_donation: DonationNode | None = None, error_message: str = "". ## Goal

Build the AI helper layer of a headless first-week assistant for international students arriving in Ann Arbor. ai/models.jac decides whether a model can be called: AI can be switched off for the whole process with the UARRIVED_AI_OFF environment variable, a model slot set to None is off, a real Anthropic model needs an ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and a test double is always usable. ai/guide.jac holds a swappable guide model and an LLM-backed answer_task_question that answers a student's follow-up question about one orientation task, plus guide_ready. ai/translate.jac holds a swappable translator model and LLM-backed translate, translate_post and translate_batch functions that return typed results, plus translator_ready. main.jac only imports the public names. Tests must swap the model globs for MockLLM and never call a real model.

## Module relationships

```mermaid
flowchart LR

    M2["ai/guide.jac"]
    M3["ai/translate.jac"]
    M4["main.jac"]
