2: 
3: ## Goal
4: 
5: Build the headless backend of Trace, a disaster-response incident graph where every status about a person comes from a cited source. graph/nodes.jac defines the graph records (Incident, Person, Claim, Source, Organization, Media, Location, VerificationSignal, Subscription, Alert, ActivityEntry, InvestigationRun, identity-review records). graph/edges.jac defines typed relationships. graph/activity.jac provides now_iso, plain_status and log_activity. services/timeline.jac exposes person_timeline(incident_id, person_id), a read-only cited history for one person in one incident. main.jac imports the timeline endpoint and activity helpers. Tests cover timeline ordering, linked alerts and runs, incident scoping, plain status wording and activity logging.
6: 
7: Target: Jac 0.36.1, backend-only service (no JSX, no browser UI, no external AI). Jac 0.36.1 infers placement, so no cl/sv markers are used.
8: 
9: ## Module relationships
10: 
11: ```mermaid
12: flowchart LR
13:     M1["graph/nodes.jac"]
14:     M2["graph/edges.jac"]
15:     M3["graph/activity.jac"]
16:     M4["services/timeline.jac"]
17:     M5["main.jac"]
18:     M1 --> M2
19:     M1 --> M3
20:     M1 --> M4
21:     M2 --> M4
22:     M4 --> M5
23:     M3 --> M5
24: ```
25: 
26: An arrow points from a provider to a module that imports it.
27: 
28: ## Frontend modules (.jac)
29: 
30: None (headless backend).
31: 
32: ## Backend modules (.jac)
33: 
34: - `graph/nodes.jac` - Trace graph records, no local imports. Ids come from jid(); timestamps are ISO strings. Public interface: `Incident`, `Person`, `Claim`, `Organization`, `Source`, `Media`, `Location`, `VerificationSignal`, `Subscription`, `Alert`, `IdentityReviewEntry`, `IdentityDecision`, `IdentityProposal`, `ActivityEntry`, `InvestigationRun`, `MediaMetadata`, `MediaComment`, `MediaAssertion`.
35: - `graph/edges.jac` - Imports node types from graph/nodes.jac and declares typed edges: Involves Incident->Person, Contains Incident->Media, Asserts Source->Claim, About Claim->Person, SupportedBy Claim->Media, Depicts Media->Person, LocatedAt Media->Location, HasSignal Media->VerificationSignal, HasSubscription Person->Subscription, Receives Subscription->Alert, HasOrganization Incident->Organization, Publishes Organization->Source, HasInvestigation Incident->InvestigationRun, Triggered Claim->Alert (walker_name="WatchWalker", created_at), Reviews IdentityDecision->Person, ExactCopyOf Media->Media (hash_algo="sha256", detected_by, detected_at), ReportedAt Claim->Location, HasSource Incident->Source. Public interface: `Involves`, `Contains`, `Asserts`, `About`, `SupportedBy`, `Depicts`, `LocatedAt`, `HasSignal`, `HasSubscription`, `Receives`, `HasOrganization`, `Publishes`, `HasInvestigation`, `Triggered`, `Reviews`, `ExactCopyOf`, `ReportedAt`, `HasSource`.
36: - `graph/activity.jac` - Imports ActivityEntry. now_iso (UTC, seconds precision); glob PLAIN_STATUS (MISSING, FOUND_SAFE, INJURED, DECEASED, SEEN_AT_LOCATION -> plain phrases); plain_status falls back to lowercased code with underscores as spaces; log_activity connects a new ActivityEntry to root. Public interface: `now_iso`, `PLAIN_STATUS`, `plain_status`, `log_activity`.
37: - `services/timeline.jac` - Imports Incident, Person, Claim, Alert, InvestigationRun and Involves, About, Asserts, HasSubscription, Receives, HasInvestigation. obj TimelineEntry plus person_timeline: find Incident on root by jid, Person it Involves; claims About the person (skip other incident_id) sorted by parsed reported time, ingested time, source, kind rank; mark status_changed/previous_claim_*; alerts via HasSubscription->Receives (deduped, claim_id cited when it is one of the person's claims, subscriber names); InvestigationRuns on the incident for this person (status, mode, run_at, message, first citation claim_id from result_json). Sort, keep latest 50, set total_entries. Unknown incident/person -> []. Public interface: `TimelineEntry`, `person_timeline`.
38: - `main.jac` - Imports TimelineEntry, person_timeline from services.timeline and now_iso, plain_status, log_activity from graph.activity. No other code. Public interface: `TimelineEntry`, `person_timeline`, `now_iso`, `plain_status`, `log_activity`.
39: 
40: ## Jac module build order
41: 
42: | Order | File | Imports from this app | Public interface |
43: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
44: | 1 | `graph/nodes.jac` | - | node/obj records listed above |
45: | 2 | `graph/edges.jac` | nodes | 18 edge types listed above |
46: | 3 | `graph/activity.jac` | ActivityEntry | `now_iso`, `PLAIN_STATUS`, `plain_status`, `log_activity` |
47: | 4 | `services/timeline.jac` | Incident, Person, Claim, Alert, InvestigationRun, Involves, About, Asserts, HasSubscription, Receives, HasInvestigation | `TimelineEntry`, `person_timeline` |
48: | 5 | `main.jac` | TimelineEntry, person_timeline, now_iso, plain_status, log_activity | re-exports |
49: 
50: ## Build support
51: 
52: - `jac.toml`: [project] kind service, entry-point main.jac; no npm or AI dependencies.
53: 
54: ## Planned signatures
55: 
56: - `node Incident { has name: str, description: str = "", start_time: str = "", region: str = ""; }`
57: - `node Person { has name: str, age: int = 0, notes: str = "", external_id: str = ""; }`
58: - `node Claim { has claim_type: str, value: str = "", timestamp: str = "", notes: str = "", seen_by_watch: bool = False, incident_id: str = "", ingested_at: str = "", original_content: str = "", source_reference: str = "", extraction_method: str = "", ingestion_key: str = "", payload_hash: str = "", external_id: str = ""; }`
59: - `node Source { has name: str, source_type: str = "", url: str = "", external_id: str = ""; }`
60: - `node Subscription { has subscriber_name: str, subscriber_contact: str = "", external_id: str = ""; }`
61: - `node Alert { has message: str, created_at: str = "", severity: str = "info", claim_id: str = ""; }`
62: - `node ActivityEntry { has walker_name: str, message: str, created_at: str = "", incident_id: str = "", target_ids: list[str] = []; }`
63: - `node InvestigationRun { has person_id: str, fingerprint: str, result_json: str, created_at: str = "", mode: str = ""; }`
64: - `edge Involves`, `Asserts`, `About`, `HasSubscription`, `Receives`, `HasInvestigation` (typed by endpoints above)
65: - `def now_iso() -> str`
66: - `def plain_status(claim_type: str) -> str`
67: - `def log_activity(walker_name: str, message: str, incident_id: str = "") -> None`
68: - `obj TimelineEntry { has id: str, kind: str, person_id: str, claim_id: str = "", source_name: str = "", source_ids: list[str] = [], claim_type: str = "", reported_at: str = "", ingested_at: str = "", source_reference: str = "", recorded_at: str = "", text: str = "", status: str = "", mode: str = "", subscriber_names: list[str] = [], status_changed: bool = False, previous_claim_id: str = "", previous_claim_type: str = "", total_entries: int = 0; }`
69: - `def:pub person_timeline(incident_id: str, person_id: str) -> list[TimelineEntry]`
70: 
71: ## Scaffold write order
72: 
73: 1. docs/plan.md (this file)
74: 2. jac.toml

1: # Implementation plan
2: 
3: ## Goal
4: 
5: Small headless Jac 0.36.1 document-intake backend for an eldercare assistant. A Patient node is the hub; Document nodes hang off it. Two LLM-backed abilities (classify_document, translate_to_plain_english) read their model from the module-level glob `llm`. Two walkers start at a Patient, visit its documents in connection order, and stop the whole walk (disengage) at the first document they should skip. Tests swap `llm` for MockLLM.
6: 
7: ## Module relationships
8: 
9: ```mermaid
10: flowchart LR
11:     M1["graph/nodes/patient.jac"]
12:     M2["graph/nodes/document.jac"]
13:     M3["abilities/llm_abilities.jac"]
14:     M4["graph/walkers/intake/document_classify.jac"]
15:     M5["graph/walkers/intake/plain_english_translator.jac"]
16:     M6["main.jac"]
17:     M1 --> M4
18:     M2 --> M4
19:     M3 --> M4
20:     M1 --> M5
21:     M2 --> M5
22:     M3 --> M5
23:     M1 --> M6
24:     M2 --> M6
25:     M3 --> M6
26:     M4 --> M6
27:     M5 --> M6
28: ```
29: 
30: An arrow points from a provider to a module that imports it.
31: 
32: ## Frontend modules (.jac)
33: 
34: None (headless backend; no JSX or browser UI).
35: 
36: ## Backend modules (.jac)
37: 
38: - `graph/nodes/patient.jac` - node Patient (hub). Required `name: str`; str fields default "": dob, medicare_id, medicaid_id, address, city, state, zip_code, phone, email, emergency_contact_name, emergency_contact_phone, created_at, updated_at; `primary_language: str = "English"`. No abilities. Public: `Patient`.
39: - `graph/nodes/document.jac` - node Document; every field defaulted: doc_id, doc_type, title, raw_content, raw_text, source, original_filename, mime_type, ingested_at, plain_english_summary, embedding_id, content_hash (str ""); source_channel = "email"; classification = "UNKNOWN"; processed: bool = False. No abilities. Public: `Document`.
40: - `abilities/llm_abilities.jac` - imports environ (os) and Model (jaclang.byllm.lib); `glob llm = Model(model_name="openrouter/anthropic/claude-4.6-sonnet", api_key=environ.get("OPENROUTER_API_KEY", ""))`; two body-less `by llm(model=llm)` functions with sem strings. Public: `llm`, `classify_document`, `translate_to_plain_english`.
41: - `graph/walkers/intake/document_classify.jac` - walker DocumentClassify: Patient entry visits [-->]; Document entry disengages if classification != "UNKNOWN", else classifies with source metadata dict, stores result, prints log line. Public: `DocumentClassify`.
42: - `graph/walkers/intake/plain_english_translator.jac` - walker PlainEnglishTranslator: Patient entry visits [-->]; Document entry disengages if summary != "" or raw_content == "", else translates raw_content[:4000] with content_type=classification, reading_level=6, stores summary, prints log line. Public: `PlainEnglishTranslator`.
43: - `main.jac` - thin entry: imports only. Public: none.
44: 
45: ## Public interfaces
46: 
47: - `node Patient { has name: str, dob: str = "", ..., primary_language: str = "English", created_at: str = "", updated_at: str = ""; }`
48: - `node Document { has doc_id: str = "", ..., classification: str = "UNKNOWN", processed: bool = False, ...; }`
49: - `glob llm = Model(...)`
50: - `def classify_document(raw_text: str, source_metadata: dict) -> str by llm(model=llm);`
51: - `def translate_to_plain_english(technical_content: str, content_type: str, reading_level: int = 6) -> str by llm(model=llm);`
52: - `walker DocumentClassify { can start with Patient entry; can classify with Document entry; }`
53: - `walker PlainEnglishTranslator { can start with Patient entry; can translate with Document entry; }`
54: 
55: ## Dependency / write order
56: 
57: 1. jac.toml (support)
58: 2. graph/nodes/patient.jac
59: 3. graph/nodes/document.jac
60: 4. abilities/llm_abilities.jac
61: 5. graph/walkers/intake/document_classify.jac
62: 6. graph/walkers/intake/plain_english_translator.jac
63: 7. main.jac
64: 8. tests (tests/test_intake.jac) after bodies are implemented
65: 
66: ## Verification
67: 
68: - `jac check main.jac` and each module.
69: - Tests: `import abilities.llm_abilities as m; m.llm = MockLLM(model_name="mockllm", config={"outputs": [...]})`, build Patient ++> Documents, spawn walkers, assert classification / plain_english_summary values, disengage-stops-walk behavior, and chained two-walker run consuming consecutive outputs.
70: - `jac test` on the test file.
71: 
72: ## Revisions
73: 
74: (none yet)

The document-intake backend is complete. `jac test tests/test_intake.jac` passed 5 of 5 tests with MockLLM, and `jac check main.jac` passed.

What works:
- **Nodes:** `Patient` (graph/nodes/patient.jac) is the hub, with `Document` nodes (graph/nodes/document.jac) connected to it. A new document starts with classification `UNKNOWN` and an empty `plain_english_summary`.
- **AI abilities:** abilities/llm_abilities.jac holds the module-level `glob llm` and two `by llm(model=llm)` functions, `classify_document` and `translate_to_plain_english`. Tests replace the model by assigning `m.llm = MockLLM(...)`.
- **DocumentClassify** (graph/walkers/intake/document_classify.jac) starts at a Patient and visits its documents in connection order. It stores the model's category on each `UNKNOWN` document. At the first document that is already classified, it stops the whole walk without calling the model.
- **PlainEnglishTranslator** (graph/walkers/intake/plain_english_translator.jac) stores the model's summary on documents that have `raw_content` and no summary. It stops the whole walk at the first document with empty content or an existing summary.
- **main.jac** only imports the modules.

Each acceptance check has a passing test:
- Classification follows connection order.
- Classify stops at the first already-classified document; the unused MockLLM output proves no model call was made.
- The translator stores the summary.
- The translator stops at an empty or already-summarised document.
- Running both walkers in a row fills both fields from two consecutive model outputs.

The translator skip test checks only that later documents stay unsummarised. It does not prove the model was never called, unlike the classify skip test.

**Next steps**
- Expose the intake walkers as REST endpoints
- Add an endpoint to create patients and documents
- Mark documents processed after both walkers run

1: # Implementation plan
2: 
3: ## Goal
4: 
5: Build the headless shift-rule core of CampusSync, a scheduler for student and worker shift jobs. server/config.jac holds the hard-rule constants. server/timeutil.jac holds time helpers (times are minutes from midnight, days 0=Mon..6=Sun), including an interval overlap test. server/models.jac defines the graph nodes Employer, Employee, BusyBlock, Employment and Shift, plus the lookups employer_of, employee_of and held_shifts. server/rules.jac builds the in-memory Ledger for one week. Ledger.check returns a Verdict with an internal code, a public reason, the hours the employer may still schedule, and whether another employer is involved. The Ledger also supports clone, in-memory add/remove of held shifts, hour totals and a whole-week violations list. main.jac imports and re-exports the public names. Target: Jac 0.36.1, backend-only. Jac 0.36.1 infers placement, so there are no cl/sv markers.
6: 
7: ## Module relationships
8: 
9: ```mermaid
10: flowchart LR
11:     M1["server/config.jac"]
12:     M2["server/timeutil.jac"]
13:     M3["server/models.jac"]
14:     M4["server/rules.jac"]
15:     M5["main.jac"]
16:     M1 --> M3
17:     M1 --> M4
18:     M2 --> M4
19:     M3 --> M4
20:     M3 --> M5
21:     M4 --> M5
22: ```
23: 
24: An arrow points from a provider to the module that imports it.
25: 
26: ## Frontend modules (.jac)
27: 
28: None. This is a headless service with no JSX or browser UI.
29: 
30: ## Backend modules (.jac)
31: 
32: - `server/config.jac`
33:   - One glob statement: INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP:int = 20, MAX_DAILY_HOURS:int = 8, MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER:int = 12, WORKER_WEEKLY_LIMIT:int = 60, MIN_REST_MINUTES:int = 30.
34:   - No imports.
35:   - Public interface: `INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP`, `MAX_DAILY_HOURS`, `MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER`, `WORKER_WEEKLY_LIMIT`, `MIN_REST_MINUTES`.
36: - `server/timeutil.jac`
37:   - Imports date and timedelta from datetime only.
38:   - Globals: DAY_SHORT (Mon..Sun) and DAY_LONG (Monday..Sunday).
39:   - Helpers:
40:     - hm: zero-padded "HH:MM".
41:     - parse_hm: strips the text; a missing or empty minute part counts as 0.
42:     - slot_label: "Day HH:MM–HH:MM" with an en dash.
43:     - hours: (end - start) / 60.
44:     - overlaps: a_start < b_end and b_start < a_end. Touching intervals do not overlap.
45:     - monday_of: d minus d.weekday() days.
46:     - week_key: dflt.isoformat() when d is empty, otherwise the ISO Monday of date d.
47:     - fmt_hours: integer text when h is whole, otherwise one decimal.
48:     - g: f"{v:g}".
49:     - plural: word when n == 1, otherwise many or word + "s".
50:   - Public interface: `DAY_SHORT`, `DAY_LONG`, `hm`, `parse_hm`, `slot_label`, `hours`, `overlaps`, `monday_of`, `week_key`, `fmt_hours`, `g`, `plural`.
51: - `server/models.jac`
52:   - Graph nodes. Records reference each other by jid strings.
53:   - Imports INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP, MAX_DAILY_HOURS and MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER from server.config.
54:   - Employee methods:
55:     - first_name: the first space-separated word of name.
56:     - is_international: kind == "student" and status == "international".
57:     - cap: min(weekly_limit or 20, 20) when international, otherwise weekly_limit.
58:     - daily_max: 8 for students, 12 for workers.
59:   - Shift.hours: (end - start) / 60.
60:   - employer_of and employee_of: None for an empty id; otherwise jobj(id) if it is that node type, else None.
61:   - held_shifts(s, wk, want): the Shift nodes linked from employee s with week == wk and status == want.
62:   - Public interface: `Employer`, `Employee`, `BusyBlock`, `Employment`, `Shift`, `employer_of`, `employee_of`, `held_shifts`.
63: - `server/rules.jac`
64:   - Deterministic conflict agent and compliance checker.
65:   - Imports MIN_REST_MINUTES from server.config, overlaps from server.timeutil, and Employee, BusyBlock, Employment, Shift and employee_of from server.models.
66:   - Globals: CONFLICT = "schedule_conflict", HOUR_LIMIT = "hour_limit", NOT_ON_TEAM = "not_on_team", NOT_QUALIFIED = "not_qualified", _TIMING = [overlap, rest, daily_max], _HOURS = [weekly_cap, dept_hours].
67:   - Objects: Held, Block, Verdict and Ledger (caches keyed by sid or by sid|did).
68:   - Ledger.check order:
69:     1. No allotment gives not_on_team.
70:     2. Not qualified gives not_qualified.
71:     3. A failed conflict verdict is returned with hours_left set to hours_left(sid, did).
72:     4. Otherwise the result of compliance.
73:   - compliance order: weekly_cap, then dept_hours, then daily_max, then rest (0 <= gap < 30). All comparisons use a 1e-9 tolerance.
74:   - violations order:
75:     1. Per held shift: overlap with busy blocks, then overlap or rest against later held shifts on the same day.
76:     2. weekly_cap.
77:     3. dept_hours for each department, in sorted order.
78:     4. daily_max for each day, in sorted order.
79:   - Public interface: `CONFLICT`, `HOUR_LIMIT`, `NOT_ON_TEAM`, `NOT_QUALIFIED`, `Held`, `Block`, `Verdict`, `Ledger`.
80: - `main.jac`
81:   - Thin entry point that imports and re-exports the public names from server.models and server.rules.
82:   - No routes or UI.
83:   - Public interface: none of its own.
84: 
85: ## Jac module build order (scaffold write order)
86: 
87: | Order | File | Imports from this app |
88: | ---: | --- | --- |
89: | 1 | `server/config.jac` | none |
90: | 2 | `server/timeutil.jac` | none |
91: | 3 | `server/models.jac` | INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP, MAX_DAILY_HOURS, MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER |
92: | 4 | `server/rules.jac` | MIN_REST_MINUTES, overlaps, Employee, BusyBlock, Employment, Shift, employee_of |
93: | 5 | `main.jac` | all public names from server.models and server.rules |
94: 
95: Supporting file: `jac.toml` (project campussync, entry-point main.jac). It is written first so that absolute `server.*` imports resolve.
96: 
97: ## Planned signatures
98: 
99: ### `server/config.jac`
100: 
101: - glob INTERNATIONAL_WEEKLY_CAP: int = 20, MAX_DAILY_HOURS: int = 8, MAX_DAILY_HOURS_WORKER: int = 12, WORKER_WEEKLY_LIMIT: int = 60, MIN_REST_MINUTES: int = 30;
102: 
103: ### `server/timeutil.jac`
104: 
105: - def hm(minutes: int) -> str
106: - def parse_hm(text: str) -> int
107: - def slot_label(day: int, start: int, end: int) -> str
108: - def hours(start: int, end: int) -> float
109: - def overlaps(a_start: int, a_end: int, b_start: int, b_end: int) -> bool
110: - def monday_of(d: date) -> date
111: - def week_key(d: str, dflt: date) -> str
112: - def fmt_hours(h: float) -> str
113: - def g(v: float) -> str
114: - def plural(n: int | float, word: str, many: str = "") -> str
115: 
116: ### `server/models.jac`
117: 
118: - node Employer
119:   - name, type="department", kind="business", university, join_code, timezone="America/New_York"
120:   - default_pay_rate=15.0, default_weekly_hours=20, state_tax_pct=4.25
121:   - description, created
122:   - auto_generate=True, auto_recruit=True, auto_approve_swaps=False
123: - node Employee
124:   - name, email, student_number, kind="student", school, status="domestic"
125:   - weekly_limit=20, desired_hours=12, preferences, open_swap_days, autopilot=True, note
126:   - calendar_source, calendar_url, google_refresh_token, google_email, google_calendar_id, shifts_signature, calendar_synced_at, calendar_error
127:   - demo_events, created
128:   - methods: first_name, is_international, cap, daily_max
129: - node BusyBlock
130:   - day, start, end, title="Busy", source="calendar", week=""
131: - node Employment
132:   - student, employer, hours=10, state="invited", positions, pay_rate=15.0, created
133: - node Shift
134:   - employer, week, day, start, end, student, state="assigned", status="published"
135:   - draft, reason, source="generated", position, created
136:   - method: hours
137: - def employer_of(id: str) -> Employer | None
138: - def employee_of(id: str) -> Employee | None
139: - def held_shifts(s: Employee, wk: str, want: str = "published") -> list[Shift]
140: 
141: ### `server/rules.jac`
142: 
143: - obj Held
144:   - fields: shift_id, department_id, day, start, end
145:   - method: hours -> float
146: - obj Block
147:   - fields: day, start, end, title="Busy"
148: - obj Verdict
149:   - fields: ok, code="", hours_left=0.0, cross_department=False
150:   - methods: public_reason, is_timing, is_hours
151: - obj Ledger
152:   - fields: week, _students, _busy, _held, _allot, _has_allot, _roles
153:   - methods:
154:     - student, busy, held, _key
155:     - allotment, set_allotment, roles, qualified
156:     - clone, add, remove
157:     - total_hours, dept_hours, day_hours, cap, cap_left, hours_left
158:     - conflict, compliance, check, violations
159: 
160: ## Verification
161: 
162: - Flow: create an employee, employment and shifts on root, then Ledger.check, then clone/add/remove, then violations.
163: - Run `jac check` on every module and on main.jac.
164: - Run `tests/test_rules.jac` with `jac test`. It covers:
165:   - Employee caps, daily_max and employee_of.
166:   - Ledger.check codes: not_on_team, not_qualified, ok, overlap with cross_department.
167:   - compliance: weekly_cap, daily_max, rest.
168:   - clone isolation.
169:   - violations order.
170: 
171: ## Revisions
172: 
173: - None yet.

  - The ledger also supports `clone`, in-memory add/remove, hour totals and the ordered `violations` list.
- **main.jac:** re-exports the public names.

The tests cover employee caps and lookups, `held_shifts` filtering by week and status, the `check` codes, the compliance rules, clone isolation and the order of the violations list.

**Next steps**
- Add a walker endpoint that checks a proposed shift
- Add a schedule generator using the Ledger
- Add a swap approval flow with compliance checks

1: # Flair backend: implementation plan
2: 
3: ## Goal
4: 
5: Build the headless scoring core of Flair, a retention and engagement auditor for consumer web apps. A crawler (out of scope) produces deterministic signals. An LLM rubric evaluator turns an evidence pack plus those signals into a JSON text verdict. The service parses that verdict into a typed audit bundle with clamped category scores and normalized findings.
6: 
7: The service falls back to a bundle built from the deterministic retention signals in three cases:
8: 
9: - the LLM call fails
10: - the LLM returns text that cannot be parsed
11: - the LLM returns no findings
12: 
13: Target: Jac 0.36.1, backend only (no JSX, no browser UI). Placement is inferred, so files use no `cl`/`sv` markers. Tests never call a real model; they use MockLLM.
14: 
15: ## Module relationships
16: 
17: ```mermaid
18: flowchart LR
19:     M1["services/models.jac"]
20:     M2["services/llm.jac"]
21:     M3["services/audits.jac"]
22:     M4["main.jac"]
23:     M1 --> M2
24:     M1 --> M3
25:     M2 --> M3
26:     M3 --> M4
27: ```
28: 
29: An arrow points from a provider to the module that imports it.
30: 
31: ## Frontend modules (.jac)
32: 
33: None. This is a headless service slice.
34: 
35: ## Backend modules (.jac)
36: 
37: - `services/models.jac`: plain `obj` declarations with no imports. Every field has a default, and every obj and field has a sem description.
38: - `services/llm.jac`: holds `glob llm: Model` and the body-less function `evaluate_retention_recommendations ... by llm(max_tokens=3600)`, along with its function and parameter sems.
39: - `services/audits.jac`: clamping, the weighted rubric, the JSON payload extractor, safe JSON accessors, finding parsing, bundle parsing, the fallback bundle, and the safe orchestration entry.
40: - `main.jac`: one import of the public audit functions and no declarations of its own.
41: 
42: ## Public interfaces
43: 
44: ### services/models.jac
45: 
46: - `obj DeterministicSignal`:
47:   - `lane_retention_or_conversion`, `category`: str, default `""`
48:   - `severity`: str, default `"medium"`
49:   - `confidence`: float, default `0.7`
50:   - `page_url`, `issue_location`, `evidence_ref`, `evidence`, `proof`, `why_it_matters`, `research_basis`, `recommendation`, `fix_guidance`, `exact_ui_or_copy_tip`, `primary_metric`, `guardrail_metric`: str, default `""`
51:   - `estimated_effort`, `expected_impact`: str, default `"medium"`
52: - `obj LlmFindingDraft`:
53:   - `category`, `lane_retention_or_conversion`: str, default `""`
54:   - `severity`: str, default `"medium"`
55:   - `confidence`: float, default `0.7`
56:   - the same string fields as DeterministicSignal, from `page_url` through `expected_impact`, with the same defaults
57:   - `legal_safe`: bool, default `True`
58: - `obj LlmAuditBundle`:
59:   - `score`: int, default `60`
60:   - ten int category scores, each default `5`: `onboarding_activation`, `habit_loop_strength`, `reward_design_feedback`, `social_retention_mechanics`, `attention_capture_session_depth`, `personalization_adaptation`, `friction_reduction`, `progression_investment`, `reentry_notification_systems`, `trust_emotional_safety`
61:   - `strengths`, `weaknesses`, `retention_risks`, `highest_leverage_improvements`: list[str], default `[]`
62:   - `dark_pattern_risk_score`: int, default `0`
63:   - `dark_pattern_risk_reasons`: list[str], default `[]`
64:   - `findings`: list[LlmFindingDraft], default `[]`
65: 
66: ### services/llm.jac
67: 
68: - `glob llm: Model = Model(model_name="gpt-4o");`
69:   - `Model` is imported from `jaclang.byllm.lib`.
70: - `def evaluate_retention_recommendations(target_url: str, evidence_pack: str, deterministic_signals: list[DeterministicSignal]) -> str by llm(max_tokens=3600);`
71:   - The function and its three parameters carry their sems verbatim from the task.
72:   - It reads the module-level `llm` at call time, so tests can swap in MockLLM.
73: 
74: ### services/audits.jac
75: 
76: | Signature | Behavior |
77: | --- | --- |
78: | `def bounded_score(score: int) -> int` | Clamps to 0..100. |
79: | `def bounded_ten(score: int) -> int` | Clamps to 0..10. |
80: | `def blended_score(llm_score: int, deterministic_score: int) -> int` | Returns `bounded_score((bounded_score(a) + bounded_score(b)) // 2)`. |
81: | `def rubric_overall(bundle: LlmAuditBundle) -> int` | Weighted sum of the ten `bounded_ten` category scores, then `bounded_score(int((w / 10.8) * 10.0))`. |
82: | `def draft_from_signal(signal: DeterministicSignal) -> LlmFindingDraft` | Copies the 18 shared fields and sets `legal_safe=True`. |
83: | `def fallback_bundle(lane: str, signals: list[DeterministicSignal], score: int) -> LlmAuditBundle` | Builds the deterministic fallback bundle described below. |
84: | `def llm_json_payload(text: str) -> str` | Strips code fences and surrounding prose; returns the span from the first `{` to the last `}`. |
85: | `def json_str(data: any, key: str, fallback_value: str) -> str` | Safe accessor; falls back if the key is missing or the value is `"None"`. |
86: | `def json_int(data: any, key: str, fallback_value: int) -> int` | Safe accessor. |
87: | `def json_float(data: any, key: str, fallback_value: float) -> float` | Safe accessor. |
88: | `def json_bool(data: any, key: str, fallback_value: bool) -> bool` | Safe accessor. |
89: | `def json_string_list(data: any, key: str) -> list[str]` | Safe accessor; returns the items collected before any error. |
90: | `def bounded_confidence(value: float) -> float` | Clamps to 0.0..1.0. |
91: | `def parse_llm_findings(data: any) -> list[LlmFindingDraft]` | Parses findings as described below. |
92: | `def parse_llm_bundle(result: str, signals: list[DeterministicSignal], score: int) -> LlmAuditBundle` | Parses the model text as described below. |
93: | `def safe_retention_bundle(target_url: str, evidence_pack: str, signals: list[DeterministicSignal], score: int) -> LlmAuditBundle` | Calls the evaluator, parses the result, and falls back on any exception. |
94: 
95: Rubric weights used by `rubric_overall`:
96: 
97: | Category | Weight |
98: | --- | ---: |
99: | onboarding_activation | 1.0 |
100: | habit_loop_strength | 1.2 |
101: | reward_design_feedback | 1.1 |
102: | social_retention_mechanics | 1.0 |
103: | attention_capture_session_depth | 1.1 |
104: | personalization_adaptation | 1.2 |
105: | friction_reduction | 1.1 |
106: | progression_investment | 1.2 |
107: | reentry_notification_systems | 1.0 |
108: | trust_emotional_safety | 0.9 |
109: 
110: `fallback_bundle` behavior:
111: 
112: - Findings are `draft_from_signal` of each signal whose lane matches, in input order.
113: - If no signal matches, it uses one baseline finding:
114:   - category "baseline opportunity", severity "medium", confidence 0.55
115:   - estimated_effort "low", expected_impact "medium"
116:   - primary_metric is the lane followed by " score"
117:   - guardrail_metric "support tickets and complaint rate"
118: - Every category gets a value of 3 if the score is below 40, 7 if the score is above 75, and 5 otherwise.
119: - The bundle score is the given score, unchanged.
120: - `weaknesses`, `retention_risks` and `highest_leverage_improvements` each hold one sentence.
121: 
122: `parse_llm_findings` behavior:
123: 
124: - Every finding is forced into the `"retention"` lane.
125: - Defaults:
126:   - category "retention loop", severity "medium"
127:   - confidence 0.7, clamped
128:   - primary_metric "repeat sessions", guardrail_metric "complaints and opt-outs"
129:   - estimated_effort "medium", expected_impact "medium"
130:   - legal_safe True
131:   - all other string fields ""
132: - If an error occurs, it returns the findings parsed so far.
133: 
134: `parse_llm_bundle` behavior:
135: 
136: - It runs `json.loads` on the result of `llm_json_payload`. Parse errors propagate to the caller.
137: - If no findings are parsed, it returns `fallback_bundle("retention", signals, score)`.
138: - Otherwise the score is clamped to 0..100, each category is clamped to 0..10 with default 5, and the list fields are read with `json_string_list`.
139: - `dark_pattern_risk_score` is `bounded_ten`, with default 0.
140: 
141: ### main.jac
142: 
143: - `import from services.audits { safe_retention_bundle, parse_llm_bundle, fallback_bundle, rubric_overall, blended_score }`
144: 
145: ## Scaffold write order
146: 
147: 1. `docs/plan.md`
148: 2. `jac.toml` (support file: [project] name flair-backend, entry-point main.jac, no extra tables)
149: 3. `services/models.jac`
150: 4. `services/llm.jac`
151: 5. `services/audits.jac` (every body is `raise NotImplementedError();` during scaffold)
152: 6. `main.jac`
153: 7. `tests/test_audits.jac`
154: 
155: ## Verification
156: 
157: Flow: signals and evidence go to `evaluate_retention_recommendations` (MockLLM), then to `parse_llm_bundle` or `fallback_bundle`, which returns an `LlmAuditBundle`. `rubric_overall` and `blended_score` then run on bundles.
158: 
159: Routes: API only; this slice has no endpoints.
160: 
161: Steps:
162: 
163: 1. Run `jac check main.jac`, then check the other modules.
164: 2. `tests/test_audits.jac` imports `services.llm as m;` and sets `m.llm = MockLLM(model_name="mockllm", config={"outputs": [...]})` from `jaclang.byllm.lib`.
165: 3. The tests cover:
166:    - fenced and prose-wrapped JSON
167:    - clamping of the score, the categories and confidence
168:    - finding defaults and the forced retention lane
169:    - the fallback for empty findings and unparsable output
170:    - the baseline finding when no retention signals exist
171:    - category values of 3, 5 and 7
172:    - `rubric_overall` and `blended_score`
173: 4. Run `jac test tests/test_audits.jac`.
174: 
175: ## Execution notes and revisions
176: 
177: - None yet. Record evidence-based changes here.

messages.content:
1: # InsuraAgent backend: implementation plan
2: 
3: Target: Jac 0.36.1. Backend-only service. No JSX and no browser UI. Placement is inferred, so files use no `cl`/`sv` markers. Tests never call a real model; they use MockLLM.
4: 
5: ## Goal
6: 
7: Build a headless health-insurance appeal agent.
8: 
9: - `models.jac` holds the typed data model.
10: - `tools.jac` holds five LLM-backed tools. Each tool asks the model for plain text or JSON text, then parses the answer into typed objects. Parsing tolerates markdown fences and surrounding prose.
11: - `walkers.jac` exposes two public walkers:
12:   - `submit_claim` stores the claim and policy, runs the five tools in sequence, stores an Appeal, and reports the letter.
13:   - `list_appeals` reports one summary row per stored appeal.
14: - `main.jac` only re-exports the two walkers.
15: 
16: ## Module relationships
17: 
18: ```mermaid
19: flowchart LR
20:     M1["models.jac"]
21:     M2["tools.jac"]
22:     M3["walkers.jac"]
23:     M4["main.jac"]
24:     M1 --> M2
25:     M1 --> M3
26:     M2 --> M3
27:     M3 --> M4
28: ```
29: 
30: Each arrow points from a provider to the module that imports it.
31: 
32: ## Frontend modules (.jac)
33: 
34: None. This is a backend-only service.
35: 
36: ## Backend modules (.jac)
37: 
38: - `models.jac`
39:   - Imports: none.
40:   - Public interface: `DenialReason`, `AppealStrength`, `PolicyClause`, `Contradiction`, `AppealLetter`, `Claim`, `Policy`, `Appeal`.
41: - `tools.jac`
42:   - Imports: `os`, `json`, `re`, `Model` from `jaclang.byllm.llm`, and models.
43:   - Public interface: `llm`, `extract_denial_reason`, `extract_relevant_clauses`, `find_contradictions`, `assess_appeal_strength`, `draft_appeal_letter`.
44: - `walkers.jac`
45:   - Imports: `json`, `uuid`, `datetime`, models, and tools.
46:   - Public interface: `submit_claim`, `list_appeals`.
47: - `main.jac`
48:   - Contents: only `import from walkers { submit_claim, list_appeals }`.
49:   - Public interface: `submit_claim`, `list_appeals`.
50: 
51: ## Public signatures
52: 
53: ### models.jac
54: 
55: - `enum DenialReason { NOT_MEDICALLY_NECESSARY, OUT_OF_NETWORK, PRIOR_AUTH_MISSING, EXPERIMENTAL_OR_INVESTIGATIONAL, CODING_ERROR, BENEFIT_EXCLUSION, OTHER }`
56: - `enum AppealStrength { WEAK, MODERATE, STRONG, VERY_STRONG }`
57: - `obj PolicyClause { section: str, title: str, text: str, relevance_note: str = "" }`
58: - `obj Contradiction { denial_quote: str, policy_quote: str, clause_section: str, explanation: str }`
59: - `obj AppealLetter { subject: str, salutation: str, body: str, citations: list[str], closing: str }`
60: - `node Claim { claim_id, patient_name, member_id, cpt_code, date_of_service: str, billed_amount: float, denial_text: str, clinical_record: str = "" }`
61: - `node Policy { policy_id, plan_name, full_text: str }`
62: - `node Appeal { appeal_id, claim_id, policy_id: str, denial_reason: DenialReason, strength: AppealStrength, contradictions_json, letter_subject, letter_body, citations_json, created_at: str }`
63: 
64: ### tools.jac
65: 
66: Helpers and the model glob:
67: 
68: - `def _pick_model() -> Model`
69:   - Checks environment keys in this order: FEATHERLESS (uses APPEAL_MODEL, or `openai/Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct`), then ANTHROPIC, then GEMINI, then OPENAI.
70:   - If none is set, it raises an exception.
71: - `glob llm = _pick_model();`
72: - `def _parse_json_obj(s: str) -> dict`
73: - `def _parse_json_list(s: str) -> list`
74: 
75: Raw `by llm()` functions. Each returns `str` and has a docstring prompt:
76: 
77: - `extract_denial_reason_raw(denial_text)`
78: - `extract_relevant_clauses_raw(policy_text, denial_reason)`
79: - `find_contradictions_raw(denial_text, clinical_record, clauses)`
80: - `assess_appeal_strength_raw(contradictions)`
81: - `draft_appeal_letter_raw(...)`, which takes 10 arguments.
82: 
83: Public tools. Each makes exactly one model call:
84: 
85: - `extract_denial_reason(denial_text: str) -> DenialReason`
86: - `extract_relevant_clauses(policy_text: str, denial_reason: DenialReason) -> list[PolicyClause]`
87: - `find_contradictions(denial_text: str, clinical_record: str, clauses: list[PolicyClause]) -> list[Contradiction]`
88: - `assess_appeal_strength(contradictions: list[Contradiction]) -> AppealStrength`
89: - `draft_appeal_letter(patient_name, member_id, claim_number, date_of_service, cpt_code, billed_amount: float, plan_name, denial_reason: DenialReason, contradictions: list[Contradiction], clinical_record) -> AppealLetter`
90: 
91: ### walkers.jac
92: 
93: - `walker:pub submit_claim`
94:   - Fields: `patient_name`, `member_id`, `claim_number`, `date_of_service`, `cpt_code`, `billed_amount: float`, `plan_name`, `denial_text`, `policy_text`, `clinical_record = ""`.
95:   - Ability: `can run with Root entry`.
96: - `walker:pub list_appeals`
97:   - Ability: `can run with Root entry`.
98: 
99: ## Behavior rules
100: 
101: ### Mapping model answers to enums
102: 
103: The raw answer is uppercased and stripped. The first matching substring rule wins.
104: 
105: `extract_denial_reason`:
106: 
107: | Substring in answer | Result |
108: | --- | --- |
109: | `NOT_MEDICALLY_NECESSARY` | NOT_MEDICALLY_NECESSARY |
110: | `OUT_OF_NETWORK` | OUT_OF_NETWORK |
111: | `PRIOR_AUTH` | PRIOR_AUTH_MISSING |
112: | `EXPERIMENTAL` or `INVESTIGATIONAL` | EXPERIMENTAL_OR_INVESTIGATIONAL |
113: | `CODING` | CODING_ERROR |
114: | `EXCLUSION` | BENEFIT_EXCLUSION |
115: | anything else | OTHER |
116: 
117: `assess_appeal_strength`:
118: 
119: | Substring in answer | Result |
120: | --- | --- |
121: | `VERY_STRONG` or `VERY STRONG` | VERY_STRONG |
122: | `STRONG` | STRONG |
123: | `WEAK` | WEAK |
124: | anything else | MODERATE |
125: 
126: ### Parsing JSON answers
127: 
128: `_parse_json_obj` and `_parse_json_list` work the same way:
129: 
130: 1. Strip the text.
131: 2. If a ```` ```json ```` or ```` ``` ```` fence wraps the value, use the fenced content.
132: 3. Otherwise, take the span from the first opening bracket to its matching closing bracket, found by counting depth.
133: 4. Parse it with `json.loads`.
134: 5. On any failure, return `{}` or `[]`.
135: 
136: List tools skip elements that are not dicts. Missing fields become `str(d.get(k, ""))`.
137: 
138: In `draft_appeal_letter`:
139: 
140: - `citations` defaults to `[]`.
141: - A non-list `citations` value is wrapped as `[str(x)]`.
142: 
143: ### What submit_claim stores and reports
144: 
145: - Policy ID: `POL-{member_id}`.
146: - Appeal ID: `APL-{uuid4().hex[:8]}`.
147: - `letter_body` is `salutation + "\n\n" + body + "\n\n" + closing`.
148: - Report: `{appeal_id, claim_id, subject, letter, citations}`.
149: 
150: `list_appeals` reports ONE list of rows. Each row is `{appeal_id, claim_id, subject, created_at}`.
151: 
152: ## Scaffold write order
153: 
154: 1. `docs/plan.md`
155: 2. `jac.toml`, the support file: `[project]` with name `insuraagent-backend`, kind `service`, entry-point `main.jac`.
156: 3. `models.jac`
157: 4. `tools.jac`, with stub bodies.
158: 5. `walkers.jac`, with stub bodies.
159: 6. `main.jac`
160: 7. Tests: `tests/test_tools.jac` and `tests/test_walkers.jac`.
161: 
162: ## Verification
163: 
164: 1. Run `jac check` on each module and on `main.jac`.
165: 2. Run `jac test`. Tests set `OPENAI_API_KEY` to a placeholder before importing tools, then set `tools.llm = MockLLM(...)`. Outputs are given in call order: reason, clauses JSON, contradictions JSON, strength, letter JSON.
166: 3. Flow check: `submit_claim` attaches Claim, Policy and Appeal to root, then `list_appeals` reports one row per appeal.

## Goal

Build a small Jac web app for planning a spoken local weekly brief. Show the Monday that anchors the current brief week and a spoken-style week label such as "Monday, September 28, 2026" (no "Week of" prefix). Let a visitor choose a date to preview its brief week and day index. Weekdays belong to their current Monday; weekend dates belong to the upcoming Monday. Keep the date logic in a reusable service and make the page usable without an AI key.

Constraints: Jac 0.36.1, fullstack Jac app, deterministic date logic, no external APIs, no AI key.

## Module relationships

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    M1["services/brief_dates.jac"]
    M2["components/WeekPlanner.jac"]
    M3["main.jac"]
    M1 --> M2
    M1 --> M3
    M2 --> M3
```

An arrow points from a provider to a module that imports it.

## Frontend modules (.jac)

- `components/WeekPlanner.jac` - Show the current brief week, accept a chosen date, call the service walker, and render its observed response (loading, error, and default/empty states). Public interface: `WeekPlanner`.
- `main.jac` - Register the service walker and mount the planner at the home route `/`. Public interface: `app`.

## Backend modules (.jac)

- `services/brief_dates.jac` - Deterministic date logic. Public interface:
  - `def brief_monday(now: date | datetime | None = None) -> date`
  - `def brief_day_index(now: date | datetime | None = None) -> int`
  - `def brief_week_label(now: date | datetime | None = None) -> str`
  - `walker:pub preview_week { has date_str: str = ""; }` - reports `{date, monday, label, day_index, is_weekend}` or `{error}` for an unparseable date. Empty `date_str` means today.

### Date rules

- `None` means today (`date.today()`); a `datetime` is reduced to its `.date()`.
- Weekday (Mon-Fri, `weekday()` 0-4): brief Monday = `d - timedelta(days=d.weekday())`; day index = `d.weekday()` (0..4).
- Weekend (Sat/Sun, `weekday()` 5-6): brief Monday = `d + timedelta(days=7 - d.weekday())`; day index = `(d - monday).days` (Sat = -2, Sun = -1).
- Label: `f"{monday.strftime('%A')}, {monday.strftime('%B')} {monday.day}, {monday.year}"` (no zero-padded day, no "Week of" prefix).
- Acceptance example: Saturday 2026-09-26 -> `Monday, September 28, 2026`, day index -2.

[jac-skill loaded: jac-fullstack-patterns @ jac 0.34.27]

A fullstack Jac app has three layers: `main.jac` (entry), server modules (plain `.jac` files - server is the default context; `.sv.jac` is the explicit-marker option), and client components (plain `.jac` with JSX infers client). Both halves of a feature live in the same folder - see `jac-cl-organization`. Codespace placement is **inferred** (see `jac-codespaces`): JSX and string-path npm imports mark a declaration client, references pull helpers/`glob`s/imports into the bundle, and `def:pub` endpoints always stay server. `main.jac` mixes contexts naturally - server imports and endpoints first, client section below, no wrapper required (a `cl` block around the client section is the equivalent explicit form):

```jac
import from recipes.store {
    ApiResponse, RecipePayload,
    save_profile, list_recipes,
}

import ".styles.global.css";                    # string-path import -> client
import from .recipes.RecipesShell { RecipesShell }   # pulled client: app() renders it

def:pub app() -> JsxElement {                   # JSX -> inferred client
    return <RecipesShell />;
}
```

That no-argument `app()` is the single-page / manual-routing shape. With file-based routing (a `pages/` directory) `app` must instead take `children` and render it - `def:pub app(children: any) -> JsxElement { return children as JsxElement; }` - or every route is silently dropped. See `jac-cl-routing`.

## Two call styles: function RPC vs walker spawn

The client reaches the server two ways:

| | `def:pub` function RPC | walker spawn |
|---|---|---|
| call form | `await save_profile(name, email)` or `await doc_tree(version=v)` | `result = root spawn add_task(title=t);` |
| argument rule | positional AND kwargs both work - resolved against the server signature | **KWARGS only** - they map to the walker's `has` fields |
| return value | the function's return value (typed, hydrated) | a result object: read `result.reports` |

**Function RPC:** the compiled stub resolves arguments against the *server's* declared parameter names - positional args map by position, kwargs by name, and the JSON body is keyed by the server's names regardless of the caller's local variable names (verified in the emitted JS: `get_moves(game_id, r, c)` wires `r`/`c` onto `row`/`col` by position). Passing the same parameter both ways is a compile error (E5080).

**Pick the shape by whether the endpoint walks: no `visit`, no walker.** A single-`Root entry` walker that just `report`s is better written as a `def:pub` function - typed return instead of `reports[0]`, real parameters instead of `has` fields, identical `root` binding. The full rule lives in `jac-sv-endpoints`.

**Walker spawn** (the docs' primary backend pattern): kwargs fill the walker's `has` fields; everything the walker `report`s lands in `result.reports` (a list - first report is `result.reports[0]`). Both styles are async on the client - inside an async context the spawn awaits implicitly:

```
async def handle_add() {
    result = root spawn add_task(title=title);      # kwargs -> `has title: str;`
    if result.reports and len(result.reports) > 0 {  # len(), NOT .reports.length (E1030)
        tasks = tasks + [result.reports[0]];
    }
}
```

## Typed objects cross the boundary

Return `node`/`obj` instances (or `report` them from walkers) directly - no manual dicts. The compiler generates wire stubs so the client receives **hydrated typed instances**: `def:pub get_tasks -> list[Task] { return [root-->][?:Task]; }` gives the client real `Task` objects with typed attribute access. Works for `obj`, `node`, `enum`, `list[T]`, nested objects, and in both directions (typed args serialize back). Use `jid(task)` for stable list keys and identity checks - graph identity survives the wire.

## Rules

- **Name every endpoint in the entry module's import list.** `import from <feature>.X { fn, Types }` in `main.jac` is what reliably registers `fn` at `/function/fn` (walkers at `/walker/<name>`). The compile-time interop manifest is *meant* to let any endpoint a client `sv import`s self-register at server start, and often it does - but registration tracks the **exact name**, and a newly added `def:pub` in a module the entry already imports still returns **405 Method Not Allowed** until that new name joins the same import (jaseci-labs/jac#7695). Renaming it or changing its return type does not help; adding it to the entry import does. **405/404 on RPC = the name is missing from the entry-module import.** Related: an `sv import` inside the entry module's own `cl` block never registers - keep server-calling client code in separate client modules.
- **In `main.jac`: plain `import from <feature>.X { ... }`** (NEVER `sv import`). Plain = in-process import; the endpoint registers at `/function/<name>` (walkers at `/walker/<name>`).
- **In client modules (inferred-client `.jac`): `sv import` with the `sv` prefix required.** Within a feature that is the sibling form - `sv import from .store { list_recipes }` - which is the whole point of keeping both halves together. Generates the JS RPC stub. `sv import` is a **boundary fact, not placement**: it states the target module stays on the server and calls cross over RPC; the import itself lives with its client consumer. Plain `import from` to a `.sv.jac` fails the Vite build with `Could not resolve "<feature>/X.js"`.
- **Always `await` `sv import` function calls.** Stubs are `async` - `items = fetch_items()` assigns a `Promise` → silent runtime crash. `items = await fetch_items()`.
- **`sv import` from server code (e.g. in `main.jac`) declares a server-to-server microservice boundary.** Spawns a separate provider server process; session cookies don't cross → `def:priv` fails with `401 Unauthorized`. Only use for actual microservices (see `jac-sv-microservices`).
- **Import obj/node TYPES alongside functions** in both places - missing types mean a server `NameError` at runtime or lost typed attribute access on the client (`has posts: list[Post] = [];` needs `Post` imported).
- **Reader responses are cached for 60s.** The client runtime auto-classifies endpoints: **readers** (no side effects) get an LRU response cache (60s TTL, deduped concurrent calls); calling any **writer** invalidates all cached reads; login/logout clears the cache. This is why a read can look "stale" after out-of-band changes (another tab, server-side mutation) - it's the cache, not your code.
- **Write-then-refetch is the canonical mutation handler:** call the writer, then re-spawn/re-call every reader whose data it changed and assign the fresh reports into state (post a tweet, then reload feed + profile + trending). The writer call already invalidated the read cache, so the refetches hit the server.
- **Contract drift is a `jac check` away.** After editing a server endpoint's signature or types, run `jac check` across the project: a W1101 `Cannot import name` / W1051 at the stale client `sv import` or spawn line is the cross-boundary drift signal, at the exact stale line (a conventional tsc+mypy stack sees nothing across that seam). Debugging workflow: `jac-debugging`.
- **`[serve] base_route_app = "app"` serves the client at `/`.** Without it the app lives at `/cl/app` and `/` stays the JSON API index. Scaffolded client projects set it by default. The server's SPA catch-all then serves the app HTML for clean URLs (BrowserRouter), excluding API prefixes (`cl/`, `walker/`, `function/`, `user/`, `static/`).
- **Client entry is `def:pub app`** - lowercase `app`. Not `App()`, `ClientApp()`. Runtime mounts the literal name. Don't wrap it in `with entry { }`. The export is always required; its signature depends on the routing system - `app()` for manual/single-page, `app(children)` rendering `children` for file-based (`jac-cl-routing`).
- **A `cl` block is the optional explicit wrapper for the client section.** Inference already places JSX-bearing declarations, string-path imports, and the helpers they pull client (see `jac-codespaces`); wrap explicitly when you want the boundary visible in the source or need to override inference. Server is the default context, so server imports need no wrapper either way.
- **Global vs scoped CSS:** import app-wide CSS once in `main.jac`'s client section (`import ".styles.global.css";` for the Tailwind import and custom CSS variables). For component-specific classes, add a same-basename `Comp.style.css` beside the component `.jac` - it auto-scopes and needs no import. No `*` reset in Tailwind projects (breaks Preflight spacing). See `jac-cl-styling`.
- **Start with `jac start --dev main.jac`** (NOT deprecated `jac serve`). HMR reloads only client modules - server-module / `glob` changes need a full restart (endpoints and `glob`s evaluate once at server boot). Kill stale `jac start` processes first: a held port makes the new server grab the next port while Vite's proxy still points at the old one → all RPC calls fail. `pkill -f "jac start"` then restart. `jac start` exits when stdin closes - launch background/long-running servers with `< /dev/null`.
- **QA the running app with `jac browse`** (bundled headless-browser driver, no extra deps): `jac browse open localhost:8000` → `jac browse snapshot` (accessibility tree with `@e1`-style refs) → `jac browse click @e5` / `fill '#email' val` → `jac browse screenshot` → `jac browse close`. Use it to verify rendered UI and flows end-to-end, not just that the server starts.
- **Build failures print structured `JAC_CLIENT_00x` diagnostics** (001 missing npm dep, 003 client syntax error, 004 unresolved import); set `JAC_DEBUG=1` (or `[client] debug = true`) for raw Vite output. Compiled JS for inspection: `.jac/client/compiled/`.

## See also

- `jac-codespaces` - the inference rules, `sv` pinning, explicit override syntax
- `jac-scaffold` - project layout, `jac.toml`, scaffolders
- `jac-sv-endpoints` - writing `def:pub` / `def:priv` endpoints and walker endpoints
- `jac-sv-streaming` - SSE streaming endpoints: raw-fetch consumption and their registration rule
- `jac-cl-components` - writing client components + the `sv import` caller form
- `jac-cl-js-interop` - browser APIs, WebSockets, debugging compiled output

[jac-skill loaded: jac-cl-components @ jac 0.34.27] A plain `.jac` declaration carrying JSX or npm imports is client-side Jac: client placement is inferred, and the `cl` marker and `.cl` extension are optional explicit overrides (see `jac-codespaces`). Everything in this guide applies to client code however it was placed. A component is a `def:pub` function returning `JsxElement`. State = `has` fields, which compile 1:1 to React `useState` - assign directly (`x = x + 1` re-renders; no `setX(...)` call) but all `useState` semantics apply: writes are async, the closure stays stale until the next render. Mount effects = `async can with entry` (compiles to `useEffect`). Event handlers = `def` methods typed with ambient DOM events (`MouseEvent`, `ChangeEvent`, `FormEvent`, `KeyboardEvent`). No wrapper or marker needed - the JSX or npm import already places the declaration client. ## This is Jac, not React or JavaScript A client component *compiles to* React, but you **write Jac** - Python-with-braces, not JSX/JS. This is the single most common mistake: do not reach for React/JS syntax. Translate every React habit to its Jac form: | React / JavaScript (WRONG in a `.jac` file) | Jac (correct) | |---|---| | `function App() { ... }` / `const App = () => ...` | `def:pub app() -> JsxElement { ... }` | | `class X extends Component { render() {...} }` | `def:pub X() -> JsxElement { ... }` (no classes, no `render`, no `constructor`) | | `const [n, setN] = useState(0)` ; `setN(n+1)` | `has n: int = 0;` then `n = n + 1;` (direct assign re-renders) | | `useEffect(() => {...}, [])` | `async can with entry { ... }` | | `onClick={() => doThing()}` | `onClick={handle}` with `def handle(e: MouseEvent) { doThing(); }` | | `this.props.x` / `props.x` | `x` - props are plain function parameters | | `import React from 'react'` | nothing - `JsxElement` and DOM events are built-in (never import them) | | `const`, `let`, `var x = 1` | `x: int = 1;` (typed assignment) | | `=== / !==` ; `null` / `undefined` ; `cond ? a : b` | `== / !=` ; `None` ; `a if cond else b` | | `items.map(x =>
  • {x}
    • )` | `{for x in items {
  • {x}
    • }}` (statement slot) | | writing a NEW `.js` / `.jsx` / `.tsx` file | a `.jac` client component. (Pre-existing `.tsx` components CAN be imported - `import from "./components/Button" { Button }` - but never author new ones.) | If you find yourself writing `function`, `=>`, `this.`, `export`, `import React`, or a `.js` file, stop - that is JavaScript. Write the Jac form from the table above. ```jac def:pub Counter() -> JsxElement { has count: int = 0; has label: str = ""; async can with entry { count = 0; # mount effect - runs once } def handle_click(e: MouseEvent) { count = count + 1; } def handle_input(e: ChangeEvent) { label = e.target.value; } # typed via ChangeEvent return

    {"Clicks: " + str(count) if count > 0 else "Start clicking!"}

    ; } ``` ## Props Components declare props as typed function params; callers pass as JSX attributes. Type callback props with `Callable[[ArgTypes], ReturnType]` - `Callable[[str], None]` for a one-string callback, `Callable[[], None]` for a no-arg one. `Callable` is ambient (no import), and the typing catches a mistyped call (wrong arity, wrong arg type, bogus `.member`) at compile time. (The parenthesized spelling `Callable[([str], None)]` also parses; prefer the Python form.) The escape-hatch `any` disables that checking and earns a `W1037` warning; keep it for genuine interop boundaries only. Wrap incoming callbacks in a local handler so parent-side data (like a row's id) is closed over when the event fires. ```jac def:pub BookCard(bookId: str, title: str, onDelete: Callable[[str], None]) -> JsxElement { def handle_delete(e: MouseEvent) { onDelete(bookId); } return
    {title}
    ; } ``` Call site: ``. For an optional callback, type it `Callable[[str], None] | None` and guard the call: `if onDelete { onDelete(bookId); }`. **`children` needs a default.** A component that accepts nested JSX declares `children: any = None`. Nested content does NOT count as a passed attribute, so a `children` param **without a default is a required prop** - every call site that passes any other attribute fails `E1102: Component 'Card' requires prop 'children'`. (`any` is the honest type: children can be an element, string, number, or list.) ```jac def:pub Card(title: str, children: any = None) -> JsxElement { return

    {title}

    {children}
    ; } ``` **Props bundle (`props: dict`):** a single parameter literally named `props` receives the whole call-site object un-destructured - for HOCs/wrappers that just ``. The cost: per-attribute call-site validation is impossible, so the compiler emits **W5015** on the definition; suppress with `# jac:ignore[W5015]` only when forwarding is intentional. Default to named params. **`children` parameter:** always declare it `children: any = None` with `= None` default. Omitting the default makes `children` a required prop - every call site that passes no nested content fails with `error[E1102]`. Use `{children}` in the JSX body to render it. **`props: any` bundle:** `def:pub Comp(props: any)` is allowed but emits `W5015` and disables per-prop type checking. Prefer named typed parameters. Use lowercase `any` - capital `Any` is not a real Jac type; it resolves to Unknown and any attribute access on it (`props.title`) fails with a hard `error[E1032]`. **`{name}` shorthand:** when an attribute's value is a bare variable of the same name, `` expands to `title={title} onDelete={onDelete}`. Pure sugar - the type-checker validates it per-attribute exactly like the explicit form. Distinct from the spread, which forwards a whole object: use `{**props}` (the canonical Jac form) - the JS-idiomatic `{...props}` also works but earns a `W0063` warning ("prefer `{**expr}`"). ## Event types (ambient, no import) | Handler | Type | Access | |---|---|---| | `onClick`, `onMouseDown`, `onDoubleClick` | `MouseEvent` | `e.clientX`, `e.button` | | `onChange` | `ChangeEvent` | `e.target.value` | | `onInput` | `InputEvent` | `e.target.value` | | `onKeyDown`, `onKeyUp`, `onKeyPress` | `KeyboardEvent` | `e.key`, `e.code` | | `onSubmit`, `onReset` | `FormEvent` | `e.preventDefault()` | | `onFocus`, `onBlur` | `FocusEvent` | `e.target` | Use the matching type even when you don't read `e`; for an event not in the table, fall back to the base `Event` type. ## Built-in in client context - NEVER import these `JsxElement` (the component return type) and all DOM event types (`MouseEvent`, `ChangeEvent`, `FormEvent`, `KeyboardEvent`, `InputEvent`, `FocusEvent`, base `Event`) are Jac built-ins in client context; `Callable` is ambient as well. None need an import - `import from "@jac/runtime" { JsxElement }` or `import from typing { Callable }` is wrong and can fail the Vite build. ## Imports from `@jac/runtime` (complete list) - **Routing components:** `Router`, `Routes`, `Route`, `Link`, `Navigate`, `Outlet`, `AuthGuard` - **Routing hooks/fns:** `useNavigate`, `useLocation`, `useParams`, `useRouter`, `navigate` (NO `useSearchParams` - parse `useLocation().search`) - **Auth:** `jacLogin`, `jacSignup`, `jacLogout`, `jacIsLoggedIn`, `jacSsoLogin`, `jacSetToken` - **Forms / validation:** `useJacForm`, `JacForm`, `JacSchema` - **Error / suspense:** `JacClientErrorBoundary`, `JacAwaiting`, `ErrorFallback` - **Walker calls:** `jacSpawn` (prefer the `root spawn walker(...)` syntax - see `jac-fullstack-patterns`) - **DO NOT use:** `useState`, `useEffect` (aliases exist but `has` + `can with entry` are idiomatic) ## Effects: dependency arrays, cleanup, and the entry/exit closure split | Jac | React | |---|---| | `can with entry { ... }` | `useEffect(fn, [])` - once on mount | | `async can with entry { ... }` | same, body wrapped in an async IIFE | | `can with [dep] entry { ... }` | `useEffect(fn, [dep])` - re-runs when `dep` changes | | `can with (a, b) entry { ... }` | `useEffect(fn, [a, b])` | | `can with exit { ... }` | `useEffect(() => () => { ... }, [])` - cleanup on unmount | Multiple `can with entry` blocks in one component are fine and good for separating concerns - each compiles to its own `useEffect`, and dep-array effects (`can with [darkMode] entry`) sit alongside the mount effects. ⚠ **`entry` and `exit` compile to SEPARATE `useEffect` closures.** A handle created in `can with entry` (interval id, WebSocket, listener) is **invisible** in `can with exit` - the cleanup silently no-ops. For acquire-then-release pairs, use a single manual `useEffect` whose body returns the cleanup - and the outer lambda must NOT be annotated `-> None` (it returns a function): ```jac import from react { useEffect } def fetch_data(); def:pub Poller() -> JsxElement { useEffect(lambda { interval = setInterval(lambda { fetch_data(); }, 5000); return lambda { clearInterval(interval); }; }, []); return

    polling

    ; } ``` ## Statement slots: control flow inside JSX Every `{...}` in JSX child position is a **slot**. The compiler picks the shape from the body's first token: - **Expression slot** - `{name}`, `{user.email}`, `{}`, `{"hi" if cond else "bye"}` - renders one value. - **Statement slot** - body starts with `for` / `if` / `while` / `match` / `switch` / `with` / `try` - each JSX statement inside pushes a child into the enclosing element. This is the primary tool for dynamic children: iteration, conditional rendering, empty-state guards, and any combination of them. ```jac def:pub ItemList(items: list[Item]) -> JsxElement { return
      {if len(items) == 0 {

      Nothing yet.

      skip; # skip; ends the slot early }}

      Items

      {for (i, it) in enumerate(items) {
    • {it.label}
      • }}
    ; } ``` **Statement slot when:** control flow, multi-element rows, empty-state guards, `enumerate` destructuring. **Expression slot / comprehension when:** a single value or one-line `[
  • ...
    • for i in items]`. Caveats specific to slot bodies: - `skip;` inside a slot is the slot early-exit - it ends the current slot's accumulator (rest of *this* slot stops), **not** the enclosing function. Useful for "show empty state, stop here." Bare `return;` inside a slot is rejected (E2020) because it reads like a function-exit but only exits the slot; the value form `return expr;` is also rejected (E2019). - Inside a slot body, don't wrap inner control flow with another `{...}` - the body is already in slot mode. Write `if cond { }` directly, not `{if cond { }}` (E2023). The `{...}` wrapping is only needed when descending from a JSX element's children into slot mode. - Slot iteration that yields keyless JSX siblings earns a warning - `W2019` for a `while` loop, `W2021` for a `for` loop - add `key={...}` on the inner element so siblings keep their identity across re-renders. - A `has`-field inside a slot body is rejected (E2024). The slot body is a statement template that re-runs every render, so a `has` there would compile to a conditional `useState` and break React's rules of hooks. Declare reactive state at the component scope (the enclosing `def -> JsxElement` body), never inside a `{...}` slot. - `try { ... } awaiting { ... }` in a slot lowers to a `` Suspense wrapper (cl only; the `awaiting` body is the fallback). On `sv`/`na` the `awaiting` body is dropped with `W2020`; `finally` with `awaiting` is rejected (`E2022`). An added `except Exception { ... }` arm synthesizes a `` around it - the JS boundary catches ALL error types, so per-type dispatch and `as ` bindings aren't modeled. - **Dynamic tags:** `<@as_ className="box">{children}` picks the element tag from an expression (`as_: str` prop, dotted access, or `<@{expr}>`). Use the param name `as_` - `as` is reserved. ## Pitfalls The first four bullets below are **silent runtime bugs** (⚠) - no compile error, no obvious failure mode at runtime. Read them every time. - ⚠ **In-place mutation does NOT re-render - rebind instead.** `has` state compiles to `useState`; React only re-renders on a *new* value assignment. `todos.append(x)`, `todos[0] = y`, `d["k"] = v`, `.sort()` all mutate the existing object - the UI silently never updates. This is the #1 Python-habit bug. Rebind a fresh value: `todos = todos + [x];`, `todos = [t for t in todos if jid(t) != tid];`, `d = {**d, "k": v};`. - ⚠ **Hooks + `has` BEFORE any conditional return.** React hooks must fire in the same order every render. `if not jacIsLoggedIn() { return ; } has x: int = 0;` → white screen, no compile error. - ⚠ **Mount effects (`async can with entry`) fire even when the component returns ``.** Guard the EFFECT body with `if jacIsLoggedIn() { ... }`, not just the render - otherwise `def:priv` calls fire and return 401 silently. - ⚠ **Long-running async code reads a STALE snapshot of `has` state.** After an `await`, reading a reactive field back gives the render-time value, not the latest write - so `story = story + frame;` inside a streaming/polling loop re-appends to the same old string every iteration. Accumulate into a LOCAL and assign the whole value each step: ``` # FRAGILE - each read of reactive `story` inside the loop sees the render-time snapshot while feeding { frame = await next_frame(); story = story + frame; # appends to the SAME stale value every time } # CORRECT - local accumulator; assign the full value each iteration (each write re-renders) acc = ""; while feeding { frame = await next_frame(); acc = acc + frame; story = acc; } ``` - **`has` fields are reactive state - assign directly.** `count = count + 1` re-renders. No `setCount`. Non-default fields come before defaulted ones (E2004 - see `jac-has-fields`). - **Derived values are locals, not `has` fields.** Anything computable from props/params/hook results gets recomputed every render - so it's a local. Putting it in `has` forces a top-level write to keep it in sync, which can cascade to React error #301. Rule: `has` is only for event-driven or async values (user input, fetch results, server data). ``` has has_filter: bool = False; # FRAGILE - derived flag as state if useParams()["category"] { has_filter = True; } # written from render body has_filter: bool = bool(useParams()["category"]); # CORRECT - plain local ``` - **Server RPC import uses `sv import`** (prefix required). When the server module is a sibling in the same feature folder it is one dot - `sv import from .store { Post, list_posts }` - which is how a feature-organized app should read (see `jac-cl-organization`). Reaching another package needs the dot count from THIS file (see `jac-core-cheatsheet` for dot semantics). Plain `import from` to a `.sv.jac` breaks the Vite build. Include obj/node types too - they're needed to type your `has` state (next rule). See `jac-fullstack-patterns`. - **Always `await` `sv import` calls.** Stubs are `async` functions -- `todos = list_todos()` assigns a `Promise`, not the data → `TypeError: todos is not iterable` at runtime. Two valid async contexts: ``` # 1. fetch on mount async can with entry { todos = await list_todos(); } # 2. handler that calls sv import -- use `async def` (no event param; uses `has` field closures) async def handle_add -> None { todo = await create_todo(input_text); # input_text is a `has` field todos = [todo] + todos; } # bind as: onClick={handle_add} # if you need to pass a param: onClick={lambda { handle_toggle(item.id); }} ``` Plain `def handle(e: MouseEvent)` is sync -- `await` inside it emits invalid JS. - **Type `has` state with the imported `sv` types - `list[any]` loses the element type.** Store data from `sv import` calls in fields typed with the actual node/obj. Without it, attribute access in loops fails `E1032: Type is Unknown`. ``` sv import from .store { Post }; # 1 dot: the server half of this feature, same folder # FRAGILE has posts: list[any] = []; # E1032 on p.title in any loop # CORRECT has posts: list[Post] = []; # `p` in `for p in posts` is typed Post ``` - **Call server endpoints POSITIONAL, not kwargs.** `save(a, b)` works; `save(a=a, b=b)` sends empty body → 422. Also: the caller's variable names become the JSON keys - they must match the server parameter names exactly. See `jac-fullstack-patterns`. - **JSX ternary is Python-style:** `{X if cond else Y}`. NOT `{cond ? X : Y}` (parse error even inside JSX). Short-circuit also works: `{cond and }`. - **Iterate with statement slots, NOT `.map()`.** `items.map(...)` on a Jac list fails E1030 - use `{for x in xs {
  • ...
    • }}` (see "Statement slots" above; `enumerate` destructuring needs parens: `for (i, x) in enumerate(items)`). Inline `[
  • ...
    • for i in items]` still works for one-liners. - **Sorting for display:** client `sorted()` REJECTS an inline `key=lambda` (E1054 "no matching overload"). Use a **named key function** and **rebind** a fresh list (never `.sort()` - it mutates in place and won't re-render). Dict/`any` fields need a cast in the key fn: `def by_total(d: dict) -> float { return d["total"] as float; }` then `ranked = sorted(rows, key=by_total, reverse=True);`. (Inline `key=lambda` works in server `.jac`/`.sv.jac`, but NOT in client code.) Cheapest of all: sort on the server and return ordered data. - **Number formatting:** `f"{x:.2f}"` (N decimals) and `round(x, 2)` both work in client. A value pulled from a dict/hook subscript is `any`, so cast first: `f"${(amount as float):.2f}"`. - **Dict / hook access (`useParams()[k]`, `useLocation()[k]`, generic `[key]`) returns `any` and yields JS `undefined` for missing keys.** Since `undefined !== null` in JS, both `x is None` and `x is not None` MISS undefined - `params["id"] is not None` returns True even when `:id` isn't in the route, and `str(undefined)` produces the literal string `"undefined"`. **Use a truthy check (`if x` / `if not x`) for hook/dict values - it catches both `None` and `undefined`.** The narrowing-friendly `is not None` form is still correct for typed Optionals (`T | None` from `sv import`-ed functions, function params, etc.) where `undefined` can't appear. (Also: `params.get("id")` runtime-fails in the browser since `useParams` returns a plain JS object - always use `[key]`.) - **`unsafe_html(x)` opts out of escaping for raw HTML.** Ambient builtin (no import). `{unsafe_html(c.html_blob)}` renders the string as raw HTML via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (React) or `innerHTML` (bare-serve). Use ONLY with trusted content - the `unsafe_` prefix is the security-review marker at the call site; never wrap user input or anything that crossed an unsanitized boundary. - **Guard None/null/undefined when iterating or dotting into server data.** Runtime-only failure (`Cannot read properties of null/undefined`), nothing at compile. Single-level access is the most common crash (`total = result.total_posts;` when `result` is None), then nested access, then `songs[0]["title"]` on an empty list. Narrow (`if result is not None { ... }`), filter (`[ for s in songs if s is not None]`), or length-check (`if len(songs) > 0`) first; short-circuit in JSX also works - `{result and }`. For dicts/lists from `sv` calls, prefer truthy checks (`if result {`) over `!= None` - `!=` is deep equality (calls `Object.keys()`) and itself crashes on `null`/`undefined`; `!= None` is safe only for primitives. - **Event params are typed - `MouseEvent`/`ChangeEvent`/etc.** Annotate every handler that reads `e` with the real event type, so `e.target` / `e.key` resolve. When you genuinely don't read `e`, use the base `Event` type - not `any`, which earns a `W1037` warning (and capital `Any` is not the keyword, warning `W2001` "Name 'Any' may be undefined"). - **Inline anonymous functions in JSX use `lambda`, NOT `def`.** `onClick={lambda (e: MouseEvent) { count = count + 1; }}` works; anonymous `def (...)` is a parse error regardless of return type - `def` requires a name. Prefer named `def` methods; inline `lambda` only for trivial one-liners. - **`style` prop takes a `dict[str, object]`, not a CSS string.** `
    ` fails E1103. Use inline dict `
    `, or move styling to `className` + a same-basename `.style.css` annex (auto-scoped -- see `jac-cl-styling`). - **JSX uses `className`, curly-brace interpolation `{expr}`, camelCase events** (`onClick`, `onChange`). - **Client placement is inferred - no wrapper or prefix needed.** A declaration carrying JSX or an npm import compiles client on its own (see `jac-codespaces`); the `cl` block, `cl` prefix, and `.cl` extension are optional explicit overrides, never required to make normal client code client. In mixed-context files (**`main.jac`**, **`pages/*.jac`**) a JSX-bearing `def:pub` is placed client with no marker. - **Top-level component name is `def:pub app`** - lowercase. Runtime mounts the literal name. Its signature is set by the routing system: `app()` for manual/single-page, `app(children: any)` that renders `children` for file-based routing. Getting this wrong drops every route with no error - see `jac-cl-routing`. - **JSX comments use `{#* ... *#}`.** This is only valid **inside JSX element children** (between any opening and closing tag) - anywhere outside JSX is a parse error (E0001). The JS-style `{/* ... */}` is also a parse error in Jac JSX. `{}` (empty slot) is also a parse error - use `{#* note *#}` for a no-op placeholder. A `#` outside an expression slot is treated as **literal HTML text**, not a comment. - **Module `glob`s can hold rich data - including JSX.** `glob _BUILDS: list[dict] = [{"name": "CLI", "icon": }];` is a fine home for render-constant tables; iterate them in slots or comprehensions. `glob` is NOT reactive - anything that changes belongs in `has`. - **`jac fmt` can drop significant JSX whitespace** when reflowing mixed text + inline elements. Keep spacing that matters as explicit string children - `{" "}` between an element and text, `{" · "}` separators - those survive reformatting. ## See also - `jac-cl-routing` - `Router`/`Route`/`Navigate`/`useNavigate` patterns - `jac-cl-auth` - `jacLogin`/`jacSignup`/`jacLogout`, signup→login→def:priv chain - `jac-cl-organization` - file layout, component reuse, hook pattern - `jac-cl-styling` - Tailwind/`cn()`, semantic tokens, scoped `.style.css` annexes - `jac-cl-js-interop` - `new()` for browser objects, WebSocket, localStorage, polling - `jac-npm-packages` - `Ref[T]` fields, ref forwarding, npm imports - `jac-core-cheatsheet` - imports, lambda, ternary, error handling

{"task": {"schema_version": "1", "task_id": "claude_log_viewer_core_v1", "reference_id": "ref_rui_claude_log_viewer_store_tree", "request": "Build a small Jac library that helps inspect local Claude session transcripts. Given a Claude projects root, list project directories that contain JSONL sessions and show each project's decoded path, session count, and last activity. List the sessions in a project with their IDs and summary counts, skipping malformed JSONL records. A user message may be a string or a list of text blocks; record its first text. ## Goal

Build a small Jac 0.36.1 library for inspecting local Claude session transcripts.

- Given a Claude root, list the project directories under `<claude_root>/projects/` that contain JSONL sessions.
- For each project, report its decoded path, session count and last activity.
- List the sessions in a project with their IDs and summary counts.
- Skip malformed JSONL records.
- A user message may be a string or a list of text blocks. Record its first text.
- Count assistant `tool_use` blocks.
- Look up a node recursively in a trajectory tree.
- Find a subagent reference by node ID.
